issues_found: 2026-09-18 REPAIRED IN PLACE, THREE DEFECTS ON ONE CITATION. 25940230 is Martinez-Gonzalez MA, Salas-Salvado J, Estruch R, Corella D, Fito M, Ros E; PREDIMED Investigators, 'Benefits of the Mediterranean Diet: Insights From the PREDIMED Study', Prog Cardiovasc Dis 2015;58(1):50-60 - an OVERVIEW of the trial, not the trial report. build_nutrition_lada.py published it (a) attributed to 'Salas-Salvado et al.', who is the second author, (b) described as a 'landmark trial', and (c) sourcing 'reduced new-onset type 2 diabetes by 30% ... with extra-virgin olive oil or nuts'. THE 30% IS THE CARDIOVASCULAR NUMBER. The abstract in this repository's own cache reads: 288 CVD events, HR 0.70 for both MedDiets; and separately, for incident diabetes, 273 cases among 3,541 non-diabetic participants, HR 0.60 (0.43-0.85) for MedDiet+EVOO and HR 0.82 (0.61-1.10) for MedDiet+nuts. So the diabetes effect was 40%, not 30%, and it was significant in ONE arm only - the page asserted it for both. A trailing claim that 'PREDIMED-Plus showed sustained prevention over 6+ years' was withdrawn: PREDIMED-Plus is a separate energy-restricted trial and is not reported by this citation. Both occurrences (lines 485 and ~816) re-sourced with denominators and confidence intervals visible.

37583402.vetted_notes_2026_09_11: VETTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT INGESTED. The decisive finding is arithmetic. This meta-analysis screened 27 articles and pooled exactly TWO RCTs totalling 112 patients, reporting roughly a 30% increase in C-peptide AUC versus placebo at 52 weeks. 112 = 24 + 88: Ovalle et al. 2018 (Nat Med, n=24, adults) plus CLVer (PMID 36826844, JAMA 2023, n=88, children 7-17). No other published verapamil T1D RCT pair sums to 112. The existing external anchor, PMID 40111679 (2026 SR/MA, 8 RCTs, 1100 patients), draws its beta-cell estimate - C-peptide AUC WMD +0.27 pmol/mL - from TWO trials, and those are the same two. THEREFORE 37583402 IS A STRICT SUBSET OF 40111679 ON THE ONLY QUESTION THE VERAPAMIL PATHS TURN ON, and adds no data the anchor does not already contain. It is also the older document (2023 vs 2026). Adding it to the corpus would inflate the apparent evidence base for verapamil beta-cell preservation from one pooled dataset to what would read as three documents - this meta-analysis, the 2026 SR/MA, and CLVer itself - all commenting on the same 112 patients. That is precisely the failure the 2026-08-31 doctrine item names. CONCLUSION: the verapamil beta-cell evidence base is TWO RANDOMISED TRIALS AND 112 PATIENTS, however many review documents are counted. RECORD THE NUMBER, NOT THE DOCUMENT COUNT. Note separately that the adult and paediatric halves of that 112 point in different directions once Ver-A-T1D is included: CLVer (paediatric, n=88) was positive, and build_drug_repurposing_screen.py already records that adult Ver-A-T1D reported a NEUTRAL 12-month C-peptide primary at EASD 2025 (n=136, still unpublished in PubMed). 42598998.title: Impact of GAD-65 Antibody Detection on Antihyperglycemic Therapy in T2D
42598998.design: Retrospective observational cohort, single academic network (NE Ohio), 2021-2023
issues_found: OVER-PRECISION RISK: reports P<0.0001 for a change in non-insulin antihyperglycemic classes while the MEDIAN IS UNCHANGED (1 [0-2] before vs 1 [0-1.5] after). The significance reflects a distribution shift, not a change in the reported central estimate. Do not quote this as "GAD-65 testing reduced therapy classes" without that qualifier.
Single integrated delivery network, retrospective EMR - no causal claim available; treatment change may reflect clinician awareness rather than the antibody result.
Cohort n not stated in the abstract; 73.3% white, median BMI 26.2 - limited generalisability.
42598998.usable_for: Descriptive evidence that GAD-65 positivity in T2D is followed by deprescribing of non-insulin agents. NOT evidence of benefit.

42577431.title: Explainable ML model for in-hospital hypoglycemia risk in LADA
42577431.relevance: MEDIUM - LADA inpatient cohort; largest LADA n in corpus
42577431.design: Multicenter retrospective, 5 Chinese tertiary hospitals, n=752 LADA inpatients, 2019-2025
issues_found: Derivation vs external validation hypoglycemia incidence differs markedly (44.8% vs 54.4%). Case mix is not exchangeable across the two cohorts; treat external validation performance as optimistic.
Tertiary-hospital inpatients only - incidence figures must NOT be read as LADA population rates (relevant to Gap #10, LADA prevalence by setting).
Retrospective; predictors are routine clinical data, so confounding by indication for insulin is unaddressed.
42577431.usable_for: LADA cohort characteristics and inpatient glycemic lability. NOT usable for prevalence or natural-history claims.

42601001.title: SGLT2 inhibition attenuates cytoskeletal/proteostatic dysfunction via AGE-RAGE
42601001.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM - downgraded from MEDIUM on vetting
42601001.design: PRECLINICAL - streptozotocin diabetic RATS (dapagliflozin, 12 wk) plus human lens epithelial transcriptomics
issues_found: PRECLINICAL, RODENT. Recorded at intake as "SGLT2i mechanism" without that qualifier. Must not be allowed to strengthen any clinical SGLT2i path.

Endpoint is LENS OPACITY / diabetic cataract - not a hub gap. The hub tracks SGLT2i in nephropathy, inflammation and cardiovascular outcomes; this is a different organ and a different mechanism (AGE-RAGE-IGFBP2-FBN1).
STZ rat model is chemically induced beta-cell ablation - a poor model for the T2D population in which SGLT2i is actually used.
42601001.usable_for: Mechanistic hypothesis generation only. Tag PRECLINICAL on any use.

42608595.title: A multi-centre study of belatacept and sirolimus for islet transplantation.
42608595.why_high: Multi-centre human evidence directly bearing on belatacept -> islet_transplant and rapamycin -> islet_transplant, both of which currently rest on single-centre / older sources.
42608595.vetting_note: Rogers NM et al., Diabetologia 2026, Australian Islet Consortium. Full abstract read 2026-08-25. Non-randomised, phase 2, multi-centre, open-label: 9 participants on belatacept/sirolimus vs 24 contemporaneous on tacrolimus/MMF. Primary outcome (freedom from hypoglycaemia + positive C-peptide + HbA1c <53 mmol/mol at 12 months) met by 8/9 (89%) vs 12 (52%). MINOR NUMERIC FLAG: 12 of the stated 24 tac/MMF participants is 50%, not 52%; 52% implies a denominator of 23, so one participant was probably not evaluable. The abstract does not reconcile this. Not disqualifying, but the control-arm denominator must not be quoted as 24 without the caveat. OVERCLAIM RISK: the authors' own conclusion 'supporting the rationale for routine use in islet transplantation' is a strong recommendation off n=9, non-randomised, open-label, 12 months. Do NOT reproduce that sentence.

Two further errors on the same entry: the paper was attributed to 'Casas/Ludvigsson' when Ludvigsson J is first author, and the result was described as 'dose-dependent C-peptide preservation' when the trial tested a SINGLE dose (4 ug x 3) and the subgroup effect was by HLA DR3-DQ2 GENOTYPE, not by dose. Re-sourced with the real numbers: primary endpoint NOT met in the full analysis set (TER 1.091, 95% CI 0.845-1.408, P=0.50); DR3-DQ2 subgroup TER 1.557 (1.126-2.153), P=0.0078 on n=29 vs 17. ALSO ADDED, because another file in this repo already knew it and this one did not: the confirmatory DIAGNODE-3 Phase 3 was closed for futility in 2026. The page was publishing a promising subgroup signal with no mention that its replication had failed. And the correction's own first draft was wrong - it claimed no GAD-alum trial in this corpus enrolled a LADA population. build_data_dictionary.py names Agardh et al., Diabetologia 2009 (PMID 19404608), n=47 adult-onset autoimmune diabetes, primary outcome SAFETY. issues_found: HEADLINE NUMBER RESTS ON n=11, AND THE STATE RECORD DID NOT SAY SO. Front Immunol 2023;14:1110544, PMC10070978 - verified live, real paper, CITR authorship (Ballou/Barton/Payne/Muller), pubtype includes NIH Extramural support. The claim recorded on 2026-09-07 was "HLA-DR matching predicts islet transplant insulin independence", which the paper does support. But the denominators, read from the abstract on 2026-09-08, are: the study screens 965 recipients and 2327 donors, then analyses 87 single-infusion recipients split into group A (HLA-DR mismatched, n=52), group B (1-2 HLA-DR matches EXCLUDING DR3/DR4, n=11) and group C (matched for DR3 or DR4, n=24). The 78% vs 24% vs 35% five-year insulin-independence contrast therefore turns on ELEVEN patients in group B. It is a retrospective registry subgroup analysis; the authors write "suggests", not "shows". Any downstream use MUST carry n=11 and must not be phrased causally. Flagged, not rejected - the finding stands, the framing did not.

42696794.vetting_notes: Vetted 2026-09-09 against the 2026-09-08 queue item, which asked whether this paper reports any measured access data before letting it near gap #6's primary-paper count. It does not. Every consequential verb in the RESULTS and CONCLUSIONS is aspirational rather than reported: the consortium 'aims to operationalize', 'aims to provide a blueprint', and reduced vein-to-vein time 'may translate into fewer patients deteriorating'. The RESULTS section describes a grant award (Innovative Health Initiative Call 7.2, Grant-ID 101194710) and the platform the consortium intends to build. No access metric, cost figure, waiting-time measurement or patient count is reported as an observation. The BACKGROUND lists access bottlenecks qualitatively (vector shortages, manufacturing capacity, production timelines, treatment cost, travel distance) but attaches no numbers of its own. The commercial-framing caveat raised at intake is confirmed and is disclosed by the authors themselves: first and last authors are Fresenius SE employees, Fresenius Kabi supplies three more, and the competing-interest statement concedes that several contributors are members of the EASYGEN consortium the paper advocates. Scope caveat also confirmed: this is European oncology CAR-T, not diabetes, so it is adjacent to gap #6 rather than inside it. USABLE FOR: a qualitative statement that European CAR-T access barriers are recognised in the 2026 literature and that decentralized point-of-care manufacturing is a proposed response. NOT USABLE FOR: any quantitative access claim, any cost claim, any vein-to-vein time, or any count of primary evidence.

41780000.title: Finerenone in Type 1 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease.
41780000.identity_verified: PubMed record fetched live 2026-09-19 via the repo's own ingest_papers.fetch_abstracts_batch; title, journal, year, DOI and publication types all read from that record.
41780000.why_ingested: FDA approved finerenone (Kerendia) for CKD associated with TYPE 1 diabetes on 2026-09-16, the first new agent for that population in 30+ years. FINE-ONE is the single trial the approval rests on. Nothing in the hub tracked finerenone before today.
41780000.do_not_overstate: Primary endpoint is relative change in UACR at 6 months - a surrogate. It is NOT a hard-outcome trial: no eGFR-decline or ESKD endpoint was met, because none was powered. Hyperkalaemia was more frequent on finerenone. Any hub text must say "reduced albuminuria over 6 months", never "protects kidneys" or "prevents kidney failure".
41780000.citable_for: albuminuria (UACR) change at 6 months in T1D CKD
41780000.not_citable_for: kidney failure, eGFR slope, cardiovascular or mortality outcomes in type 1 diabetes
41780000.vetting_note: Heerspink HJL et al., N Engl J Med 2026 (FINE-ONE). Identity verified live. THE OVER-READING RISK HERE IS THE OBVIOUS READING, and it is worth stating before any builder cites this. "Phase 3 RCT supporting an FDA approval" invites the sentence "finerenone improves kidney outcomes in type 1 diabetes". The trial does not support that sentence. n=242, duration 6 MONTHS, and the primary outcome is UACR -- a surrogate. Result: 25% greater UACR reduction than placebo (geometric mean ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.65-0.87). No hard kidney endpoint was measured. Two findings cut the other way and must travel with any citation: hyperkalemia 10.1% vs 3.3% on placebo (2 discontinuations), and eGFR fell MORE on finerenone (-5.6 vs -2.7 mL/min/1.73m2), returning toward baseline during washout. The defensible claim is "reduces albuminuria over 6 months in T1D CKD; hard outcomes untested in this population".

42738899.vetting_note: Faustman DL, Hashiguchi S, Davis M, Kuhtreiber W; Cells 2026. Identity verified live. TWO CAUTIONS, BOTH LOAD-BEARING. (1) NOT INDEPENDENT: this is the Faustman laboratory reviewing the Faustman laboratory's own multi-dose BCG trials. It is evidence of what that programme reports, not corroboration of it, and any claim sourced here must name the authorship relationship. oxidative_stress -> beta_cell.notes: Oxidative stress -> beta cell dysfunction is one of the most strongly supported mechanistic axes in diabetes. PMID 36246880 (Front Endocrinol 2022 'Oxidative stress-mediated beta cell death and dysfunction as a target for diabetes management', PMC9554708): beta cells express only ~5% of liver-cell antioxidant capacity (catalase, GPx, SOD) and are uniquely vulnerable. ROS drives loss of beta-cell identity transcription factors, dedifferentiation, and apoptosis. 2025 Chinese Medical Journal review 'Oxidative stress in diabetes mellitus and its complications' (doi:10.1097/CM9.0000000000003230) reaffirms ROS-NF-kB vicious cycle in beta-cell pathology. Mechanism is causally linked in T2D pathogenesis (glucotoxicity, lipotoxicity); RCT-level antioxidant interventions remain mixed but mechanism itself is canonical.

canagliflozin -> inflammation.validation_notes: CANVAS post-hoc mediation analysis (Sen et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2022, PMID 35635326): canagliflozin in T2D reduced urinary KIM-1, TNFR-1, TNFR-2 and MCP-1; reduction in tubular inflammation partly mediated benefit. CANVAS primary publication (Neal et al. NEJM 2017, PMID 28605608) provides core trial context. SGLT2i class systematic review (23 studies, n=1,654) shows hsCRP reduction independent of HbA1c. oxidative_stress -> T1D.notes: Oxidative stress contributes to T1D beta-cell destruction via both direct injury (beta cells have low antioxidant capacity) and immune amplification: ROS converts M2 -> M1 macrophages; NO/peroxynitrite from infiltrating immune cells damage islets; oxidative post-translational modifications of insulin create neo-antigens recognized by autoreactive T cells (Frontiers Immunology 2025 'oxidative post-translational modifications in T1D pathogenesis'). Mitochondria are involved in both the target beta-cells and the attacking T cells. PMID 21647409 (Chen 2011 Antioxid Redox Signal) reviews redox modulation potential in T1D. RATED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED rather than VALIDATED because mechanistic plausibility is strong but RCT-level antioxidant trials (e.g., nicotinamide ENDIT, vitamin E) have NOT shown T1D prevention or beta-cell preservation. Pathway is real; therapeutic translation remains negative.

NLRP3_inflammasome -> T2D.notes: Strongly validated mechanistic link. PMID 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 Cardiovasc Res) reviews NLRP3 in T2D/atherosclerosis. PMID 17429083 (Larsen NEJM 2007): anakinra (IL-1RA) improved beta-cell function in T2D in 13-wk RCT -- proof of concept for IL-1beta pathway. NLRP3-IL-1beta-IRS axis disrupts insulin signaling. Donath group ongoing T2D inflammasome trials. Mechanism: obesity activates NLRP3 in adipose macrophages -> IL-1beta -> IRS serine phosphorylation -> insulin resistance. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 review). Anakinra NEJM 2007 (Larsen) cited but PMID not directly confirmed in search; mechanistic link well-supported by multiple reviews.

Treg_expansion -> T1D.validation_notes: 2026-06-13 web re-validation: Treg expansion is mechanistically real but clinical beta-cell preservation NOT robustly demonstrated. T-Rex phase 2 RCT (PMID 38718135, Sci Transl Med 2024): single-dose autologous polyclonal expanded Tregs were SAFE but did NOT preserve residual beta-cell function vs placebo. 2025 systematic review & meta-analysis (PMID 41267047, BMC Endocr Disord, 19 studies) found a paradoxical dissociation -- immunotherapy/low-dose IL-2 expands Tregs and can preserve C-peptide as a biomarker without consistent HbA1c benefit. Remains PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: target engagement (Treg expansion) confirmed; durable clinical beta-cell preservation from Treg expansion alone unproven.

rituximab -> T1D.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 + Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr extension: rituximab delays C-peptide loss ~8 mo but does not arrest beta-cell decline.

rituximab -> nephropathy.validation_notes: Path is a co-occurrence artifact from PMID 19940299 (Pescovitz NEJM 2009 — rituximab in new-onset T1D), where "diabetic nephropathy" is mentioned only as a T1D complication, NOT as a treatment indication for rituximab. Web validation 2026-05-03: rituximab is well-established for MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY (PMID 35074299: meta-analysis of 11 trials, n=723, significant remission improvement) and other primary glomerular diseases (minimal change, lupus nephritis), but NOT for diabetic kidney disease. Multiple membranous nephropathy trials specifically EXCLUDE diabetic patients to avoid confounding. No RCT or systematic review evidence supports rituximab in diabetic nephropathy. RECOMMENDATION: drop this path from drug-repurposing dashboards or label explicitly as "membranous nephropathy (non-diabetic)" with a separate path. The rituximab -> T1D and rituximab -> beta_cell paths remain PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

rituximab -> beta_cell.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): single course of rituximab in new-onset T1D significantly preserved C-peptide AUC vs placebo at 12 months, lower HbA1c, less insulin. Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr follow-up (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline by 24-30 months parallels controls; cumulative effect = 8.2-month delay in beta-cell decline; effect wanes — does not arrest underlying autoimmunity. Beese BMC Medicine 2025 NMA (PMID 40598585): rituximab is among 11/42 interventions with significantly higher C-peptide at 12 months vs placebo, but ranks below teplizumab and low-dose ATG in cross-trial comparisons. Conclusion: rituximab partially preserves beta-cell function transiently but does not arrest beta-cell destruction. Effect is real but modest and time-limited. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: same evidence base as rituximab -> T1D path.

teplizumab -> T1D.validation_notes: Teplizumab delays progression from Stage 2 to Stage 3 T1D by a median of ~2 years (Herold et al. NEJM 2019, PMID 31180194; TN-10 extended follow-up) and preserves C-peptide / reduces HbA1c in newly diagnosed T1D (PROTECT NEJM 2023, PMID 37861217). 2025-2026 real-world data replicate the signal: Diabetologia 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s00125-025-06646-6, 30 treated vs 10 controls), Mahesh et al. Diabetes Obesity & Metabolism 2026 (DOI 10.1111/dom.70354, only ~17% of 42 Stage 2 cases progressed to insulin in first year), and PMID 39949173 (2025 caregiver/adult real-world experiences). A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=754) reports preserved C-peptide, reduced HbA1c, and insulin-initiation delay up to 24 months. Confidence HIGH. | RE-VALIDATED 2026-08-11 (long-term follow-up angle): TN-10 Extension (ADA 2025 abstract db25-840-P, DOI 10.2337/db25-840-P) followed former TN-10 participants who progressed to Stage 3 — reaffirms delay-of-progression signal; PROTECT Extension (NCT04598893, observational, no drug) ongoing for long-term safety/durability. C-peptide preservation solid at yrs 1-2 (one or two courses); durability BEYOND 2 yrs remains an OPEN question per 2025-26 reviews. Status stays VALIDATED (HIGH) for 0-2yr; long-term durability = partially established/open. Next revalidate ~2026-09-11.

GLP1_RA -> neuroprotection.notes: DOWNGRADED 2026-08-20: VALIDATED/HIGH -> PARTIALLY_VALIDATED/LOW. This path was the single worst case found by the bare-string audit - rated HIGH confidence on zero resolvable PMIDs, and when the strings were resolved the flagship citation turned out to be a NEGATIVE TRIAL. ELAD (PMID 41326666) missed its primary endpoint (P = 0.14) and was null on both functional/global secondaries (ADCS-ADL P = 0.65, CDR-SoB P = 0.81). The one positive, ADAS-Exec, rests on an unadjusted P = 0.01 across a multi-endpoint battery. The widely circulated "18% slower cognitive decline / ~50% less brain atrophy" figures are EXPLORATORY outputs reported in press coverage, not in the trials stated endpoint hierarchy - they must not be cited as trial results. The stored note previously read "2025 phase 2b liraglutide AD trial + large propensity-matched cohorts show 40-70% lower dementia incidence", which fuses a negative RCT and positive observational cohorts into one apparent body of converging evidence. The 40-70% figure comes ONLY from the cohorts. Corrected. RELEVANCE CAVEAT, separate from the statistics: ELAD enrolled participants with NO DIABETES. Its bearing on a diabetes corpus is indirect at best. What remains: one negative RCT, two observational datasets subject to confounding by indication, and one narrative review. That supports "biologically plausible, clinically unproven" - which is PARTIALLY_VALIDATED / LOW, not VALIDATED / HIGH. DECIDING EVIDENCE PENDING: EVOKE / EVOKE+ (semaglutide, phase 3, AD). Those readouts are what would move this path, not another cohort study.

SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) reduce NLRP3 inflammasome activation in renal tubular cells via (a) beta-hydroxybutyrate-induced NLRP3 inhibition, (b) accumulation of TCA-cycle immunometabolite itaconate, and (c) reduced RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated necroinflammation, leading to decreased IL-1beta/IL-18/NLRP3 expression and attenuated renal fibrosis.
SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.clinical_anchor: Downstream kidney-outcome benefit of SGLT2i is established in large trials (CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY; see Lancet 2022 collaborative meta-analysis, PMID 36351458). NLRP3-axis remains the most parsimonious mechanistic explanation but has NOT been proven to mediate the clinical effect in humans.

external_references.PMC11539899: Braz J Nephrol 2024 narrative review consolidating SGLT2i -> NLRP3 -> DKD axis
external_references.Front Immunol 2025 (1703560): Review of NLRP3 inflammasome small-molecule therapeutics in kidney disease — supports NLRP3 as DKD target

caveats: All direct mechanistic evidence is preclinical (mouse UUO model, HK-2 cells, rat STZ DKD).
No randomized clinical trial in humans has directly measured NLRP3 inflammasome activity as a mediator of SGLT2i renal benefit.
Effect size on NLRP3 read-outs varies by model (UUO vs STZ vs db/db).
SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.validation_notes: Multiple independent 2022-2025 preclinical studies show dapagliflozin inhibits NLRP3 activation in fibrotic/diabetic kidneys via metabolic (itaconate, BHB) and necroptotic mechanisms. Narrative reviews in Braz J Nephrol (2024) and Nutrients (2023) converge on same mechanism. Clinical DKD benefit of SGLT2i well-established separately; NLRP3 is a plausible but unproven human mediator.

audit_history.notes: First audit of Gap 1 = "Gene Therapy for LADA" (SILVER tier). Searches: "gene therapy LADA latent autoimmune diabetes CRISPR 2026 beta cell clinical trial". Findings: (1) CRISPR/Cas-based cell therapy programs for autoimmune diabetes (VCTX210A, VCTX211, CTX210A) remain T1D-focused — LADA is mentioned only as a conceptual extension. (2) 2024 Biomolecules review (PMID 37833064) covers CRISPR in diabetes broadly including MODY/neonatal/T1D but not LADA specifically. (3) 2024 AEMB review (PMID 39824586) summarizes current CRISPR-Cas diabetes approaches — again, no LADA-specific clinical trial. (4) 2023 Cells "Trojan horse" review (PMID 38139149) flags off-target and safety considerations for engineered cell products in T1D. (5) LADA β-cell-protection review (Front Endocrinol 2022, PMC9483094) argues the slower autoimmune process in LADA offers a longer therapeutic window, but proposes immunomodulation and DPP-4i — not gene therapy. Decision: retain SILVER. Gap is genuinely understudied: zero LADA-specific gene-therapy trials have initiated. Corpus has 10 PMIDs on the gap 1 cluster (via new_pmids_gaps_1_5.json) all of which are adjacent (T1D CRISPR, LADA pathogenesis) rather than direct. Not promotion_candidate — need an independent secondary source evaluating gene therapy feasibility in LADA specifically (none found).

audit_history.notes: SECOND COMPLETED EQUITY RCT IN THREE WEEKS - the premise of this GOLD tier is now falsified twice. PMID 42478360 (Circulation 2026 Aug 18;154(7):624-635; NCT05407376): medically tailored groceries vs usual care in 460 Medicaid-insured adults with T2D (85.2% Hispanic, 58% food-insecure, baseline HbA1c 9.40). HbA1c treatment difference -0.40 points (95% CI -0.73 to -0.08; P=0.016); food security OR 2.12 (1.13-3.99), nutrition security OR 3.65 (1.84-7.25); hypertension and BMI unchanged. This follows PMID 41587834 (Ann Fam Med 2026, n=186, 0.7 pp) found on 2026-08-16. TWO independent completed equity-focused RCTs with concordant direction and a ~1.75x disagreement in magnitude. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is narrower than what the GOLD tier currently asserts: both are 6-month, single-country, surrogate-endpoint (HbA1c) trials with no hard outcomes and no durability data. RECOMMENDATION, REPORTED NOT APPLIED: the gap statement should be re-scoped from "no completed equity RCT" to "no equity RCT with hard outcomes or durability beyond 6 months", and the tier reconsidered against the re-scoped statement. Re-tiering a published GOLD gap is a human call.

Gap 3 (Insulin Resistance in Islet Transplant, GOLD). 2025-2026 islet-transplant literature focuses on encapsulation, hypoimmune engineering, and stem-cell-derived islets (Wang J Diabetes 2025 10.1111/1753-0407.70048 immune protection; Lee WIREs Nanomedicine 2025 10.1002/wnan.70016 micro/nano encapsulation; Diabetes 2025 cell-replacement review 74:1068; Frontiers in Immunology 2025 hPSC-derived islets challenges). Older mechanistic finding (PMID 24085506) showed insulin sensitivity actually IMPROVES post-transplant under glucocorticoid-free regimens, and contemporary regimens with low-dose tacrolimus+sirolimus do not appear to induce clinical IR. However, no 2025-2026 study systematically quantifies insulin sensitivity trajectories in stem-cell-derived islet recipients (zimislecel/VX-880, Sana hypoimmune, Vertex VX-264). Gap remains GOLD: as new modalities (encapsulated, gene-edited, allogeneic stem-cell-derived) enter trials, the IR question deserves prospective measurement. Next audit: 2026-06-06.

audit_history.action: Retain GOLD. The gap is REINFORCED, not narrowed.
audit_history.finding: Gap #3 asks whether insulin resistance is measured in islet transplant recipients. PMID 42608595 is exactly the kind of study that could have closed it -- multi-centre, prospective, two immunosuppression regimens, 12-month follow-up -- and it reports freedom from hypoglycaemia, C-peptide, HbA1c, Igls criteria, BETA-2 score, insulin requirements, allosensitisation and immune-cell subsets. It does NOT report insulin sensitivity, HOMA-IR, clamp data or any direct measure of insulin resistance. So a 2026 multi-centre islet study still did not measure the thing this gap is about. That is positive evidence for the gap's continued validity, not merely absence of evidence. Note the mechanistic relevance the study does supply: renal function was preserved only under the calcineurin-sparing regimen, and calcineurin inhibitors are independently diabetogenic and beta-cell toxic (validated path calcineurin -> islet_transplant), so regimen choice plausibly shifts insulin sensitivity -- which makes the absence of measurement more consequential, not less.

audit_history.finding: EVERY PRIOR AUDIT OF THIS GAP SEARCHED A WINDOW THAT EXCLUDED ITS OWN COUNTEREVIDENCE. All recorded sweeps (2026-08-12, 2026-08-25 and earlier) were run 2020+ and reported that only insulin-INDEPENDENCE and glycemic-control endpoints exist. Re-run all-time on 2026-09-05, PubMed returns two human PRIMARY studies in which insulin sensitivity is the measured endpoint in islet transplant recipients: PMID 24085506 (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2013, 'Improvement in insulin sensitivity after human islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes', pubtype Clinical Trial, NIH-funded) and PMID 24691031 (Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 2014, 'Insulin sensitivity index in type 1 diabetes and following human islet transplantation: comparison of the minimal model to euglycemic clamp', Comparative Study, NIH-funded). Neither appears in this gap's paper list. Measured counts, all-time: 'islet transplantation' AND (insulin sensitivity OR insulin resistance) AND humans[mh] = 74; AND (euglycemic clamp OR hyperinsulinemic OR HOMA-IR) AND humans[mh] = 15. The 2020+ window returns 77 for the looser query but the two clamp-endpoint human trials are both pre-2020, so a date-bounded sweep could never see them.
audit_history.second_finding: THE GAP'S OWN EVIDENCE DOES NOT SPEAK TO THE GAP'S OWN QUESTION. gap_evidence.json rates #3 GOLD on PMID 42608595 (belatacept/sirolimus, Diabetologia 2026). All four extracted 'findings' for that paper concern immunosuppression regimens, monocyte/NK/T/B subsets and Treg proportions. None mentions insulin resistance or insulin sensitivity. This is the 2026-08-30 PRIMARY_THIN concern reached from the opposite direction: not 'is the evidence primary' but 'is the evidence about this'.
audit_history.recommendation: Two separable actions for a human. (1) Add 24085506 and 24691031 to Gap #3's paper set and restate the gap precisely - the defensible claim is not 'insulin resistance is unmeasured in islet transplantation' (false) but 'insulin resistance is not a reported endpoint in MULTI-CENTRE / REGISTRY islet transplant outcome studies' (supported). (2) Decide whether a GOLD tier survives that restatement.

audit_history.notes: Gap #8 audit (prev 2026-08-03). MATERIAL NEGATIVE READOUT, AND THE STATE WAS FIVE MONTHS STALE. The 2026-08-03 note listed DIAGNODE-3 (Diamyd/retogatein, intralymphatic rhGAD65, HLA DR3-DQ2 stratified) as a pending ~2026 readout to watch. It had already failed: Diamyd announced on 2026-03-27 that the pre-specified interim efficacy analysis on C-peptide in the first 174 of 321 participants missed the primary endpoint with no observable C-peptide preservation and did not meet the pre-specified continuation criteria; the company then confirmed futility and DISCONTINUED the trial and opened a strategic review (April 2026). No safety concerns were reported. Consequence for this gap: the largest active antigen-specific immunotherapy programme adjacent to LADA has now read out negative in recent-onset T1D, which weakens rather than strengthens the GAD-alum arm of the LADA immunomodulator case. The LADA-specific GAD-alum+VitD pilot NCT04262479 (Phase 2, COMPLETED per registry, n=14) still has no published primary readout. Retain SILVER - the gap (no LADA-specific immunomodulator RCT) is unchanged and if anything more open - but the watch list must drop DIAGNODE-3 as pending. ACTION TAKEN THIS RUN: the GAD-alum entry in build_data_dictionary.py claimed 'Preserves C-peptide at 20 mcg dose over 5 years in LADA' and 'Phase 3 trial completed; 20 mcg preserves C-peptide 5yr', citing PMID 22296077 (Ludvigsson, NEJM 2012). That paper is a NEGATIVE Phase 3 in recent-onset T1D in 10-20 year olds (stimulated C-peptide declined similarly in all groups; primary outcome at 15 months P=0.10) - wrong population, wrong duration, wrong direction. Rewritten to cite the study that actually supports the residual claim (PMID 19404608, Agardh 2009 Diabetologia, Phase 2, n=47 GADA-positive adults, PRIMARY OUTCOME SAFETY, no significant 5-year fasting C-peptide decline in the 20 mcg n=8 and 100 mcg n=9 arms, no between-group efficacy comparison reported, 500 mcg arm declined like placebo) and to state the Ludvigsson and DIAGNODE-3 negatives explicitly.

HUMAN CALL, AND THIS ONE CONSOLIDATES SEVEN OTHERS. The P1 queue has held 6-7 untouched HUMAN CALL items since 2026-08-20 and each daily run has added another rather than resolving any. Read together they are not seven questions, they are ONE question asked seven ways: SHOULD A RANKING, A TIER OR A HEADLINE COUNT BE DERIVED FROM HOW MANY CITATIONS EXIST, OR FROM WHAT DESIGN THEY CARRY? (a) 2026-08-20 dose_response: 192 of 414 headline data points are bare dose labels. (b) 2026-08-21: 29 of 47 paths went hollow when regex artifact was removed. (c) 2026-08-22/28/29 verapamil: the #4 and #5 paths rest on a PROTOCOL while a real RCT (36826844, CLVer) sits unused in the library. (d) 2026-08-27: one insulin-pricing review carries 91 claims. (e) 2026-08-29: the Bayesian prior is 62.3% discordant with study design. (f) 2026-08-30: three GOLD/SILVER gaps rest on one primary paper each. (g) 2026-08-31 (today): RESEARCH_DOCTRINE.md's own GOLD exemplar counted three documents that all comment on ONE 12-patient phase 1-2 trial as three independent sources. ANSWER (g) FIRST. It is the cheapest and it governs the rest: the doctrine defines GOLD as "three independent sources", and today showed the definition permits counting one study three times. Fix the definition - require independent DATA, not independent documents - and (a) through (f) mostly follow from it instead of needing six separate rulings. A single ruling on the definition unblocks the queue; seven separate rulings is why it has not moved in eleven days.

DECIDE WHETHER dose_response BELONGS IN THE HEADLINE CORPUS COUNT. All 192 dose_response extractions - 46% of the 414 data points the site advertises - are bare dose labels ("360 mg verapamil", "120 mg tablets", "10 mg of dapagliflozin"). ZERO carry an outcome or mechanism token. Knowing which doses a trial used is legitimate metadata, but counting it as "evidence extracted from the corpus" overstates the evidentiary base by roughly half. Recommended: split the headline into "N findings + M dose/protocol descriptors" rather than one blended figure. This is a presentation decision with a credibility cost either way, so it needs a human call - an unattended run should not unilaterally restate the corpus headline.

HUMAN CALL, NOW WITH NUMBERS: THE TWO VERAPAMIL PATHS RANK 4TH AND 5TH ON A PROTOCOL, AND THE BEST EXTERNAL EVIDENCE FOR THEM POOLS TWO TRIALS. The 2026-08-22 item asked whether paths resting on PMID 39613428 (Ver-A-T1D PROTOCOL, no results) should rank. Today they were graded NO_RESULTS by design, and an external anchor was found: PMID 40111679, a 2026 SR/MA of 8 RCTs, 1100 patients. It supports verapamil on GLYCAEMIA firmly (HbA1c WMD -0.45%, 7 trials) and on BETA-CELL PRESERVATION weakly (C-peptide AUC WMD +0.27 pmol/mL from 2 trials). Ver-A-T1D results remain unpublished in PubMed as of today. Three options and none is obviously right: (a) keep the paths, re-source them to 40111679 and re-rank them below the PRIMARY paths; (b) split them into verapamil->glycaemia (supported) and verapamil->beta_cell (thin); (c) suspend them until Ver-A-T1D publishes. This is a scientific framing decision, not a data-repair task.

HUMAN CALL, AND THE ANSWER MAY ALREADY BE IN THE LIBRARY: THE VERAPAMIL PATHS GRADE NO_RESULTS WHILE THE CORPUS HOLDS A RANDOMISED TRIAL OF THE SAME QUESTION. verapamil->T1D and verapamil->beta_cell cite exactly one paper, PMID 39613428, the Ver-A-T1D PROTOCOL, which is why they grade NO_RESULTS - and that protocol is the single largest contributor to the whole corpus at 15 of 232 live extractions. Meanwhile PMID 36826844 (CLVer, JAMA 2023, double-blind RCT, n=88, children 7-17, 52-week C-peptide, verapamil preserved beta-cell function) IS in the paper library with an abstract, is cited in build_drug_repurposing_screen.py prose, and supplies ZERO extractions to any path. The repo holds measured evidence on its own headline question and no path uses it. Note the screen prose also records that adult Ver-A-T1D reported a NEUTRAL 12-month C-peptide primary at EASD 2025 (n=136), unpublished in PubMed - so pediatric positive and adult neutral must be presented together. Decide: (a) re-source both paths onto 36826844 + external SR/MA 40111679 and re-grade; (b) split into verapamil->glycaemia (supported) and verapamil->beta_cell (pediatric only, adult neutral); (c) suspend until Ver-A-T1D publishes. This is a scientific framing call, but option (a) no longer requires new evidence - only a decision.

HUMAN CALL: SHOULD THE BAYESIAN PRIOR ENCODE STUDY DESIGN? statistical_analysis.py sets the prior from data_point_count and PMID count alone. Measured 2026-08-29: 62.3% of comparable ordered pairs on the published page are discordant with study design, 16 pairs rank a NO_RESULTS path above a PRIMARY one. The page now DISCLOSES this in full above the ranking and caps NO_RESULTS at strength INSUFFICIENT, but the number itself is unchanged, because refitting a published probability is a modelling decision and an unattended run should not make it quietly. Options: (a) leave the prior and rely on disclosure; (b) add a design multiplier (e.g. NO_RESULTS x0.25, NARRATIVE x0.5, SYNTHESIS x0.9, PRIMARY x1.0) and version the change; (c) stop publishing a posterior for paths whose design tier is NO_RESULTS or UNGRADED. Note (b) and (c) both depend on a tier that is itself 37% blind - see the pubtype item below.

EXTEND THE PROVENANCE GATE BEYOND THE 180-CHAR LOOKBACK. The new PROJECTED_NOT_MEASURED / ATTRIBUTED_TO_OTHER_STUDY rules in extract_corpus_data.py read only the 180 characters before a match, which is about one sentence plus its lead-in. That was enough to catch PMID 36643381 publishing a power-calculation assumption ("we estimated that hs-CRP is suppressed to 3.22 mg/L") and another trial's result ("the previous report indicating that colchicine 1 mg for 4 weeks reduced hs-CRP by about 60%") as its own findings. It will NOT catch attribution that opens a paragraph and governs several sentences. Better signal available: section_type. A number in INTRO or a rationale section is almost never a finding of the paper reporting it. Measure before applying - INTRO is also where some papers state their own headline result.

run_history.summary: THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS RUN IS THAT THE QUEUE WAS WRONG, AND ACTING ON IT WOULD HAVE DESTROYED CORRECT CITATIONS. The P1 item instructed a sweep of PMID 29710129 on the basis that the paper 'contains NOTHING else: no drug price', with a recorded total of $750,000 of which $400,000-450,000 non-drug. That is false. The paper DOES state the tisagenlecleucel $475,000 and axicabtagene ciloleucel $373,000 list prices; its mean total expected costs are $510,963 and $402,647; and non-drug costs are 7% of total, about $30,000-$36,000 rising to $56,000-$60,000 with severe CRS - so the drug and non-drug figures had been inverted and inflated. Had the specified grep test been executed as written, the ten CORRECT $475K/$373K attachments in build_cart_access.py would have been withdrawn. They were retained. The state's content record for 29710129 has been corrected in place with the original text preserved. ROOT CAUSE, and it generalises: the local abstract for this PMID is a one-sentence stub because the paper is a research Letter, so the 2026-09-13 run recorded dollar figures it had no retrieved source for and graded the result LIKELY. A content record with no traceable source should be graded UNVERIFIED. THE 17065674 CONCENTRATION IS NEW AND WAS THE LARGEST REAL DEFECT FOUND: 21 live false attachments in build_lada_diagnostic_model.py, all withdrawn. The 2026-09-13 run left this PMID as the file's single unchecked provenance claim on the $1,000,000,000 screening cost. PMID 17065674 is Li, Ford, McGuire, Mokdad, Little & Reaven, 'Trends in Hyperinsulinemia Among Nondiabetic Adults in the U.S.', Diabetes Care 2006;29(11):2396-2402 - a CDC NHANES analysis of fasting serum insulin. It was cited throughout as 'DASP workshops', i.e. the Diabetes Antibody Standardization Program. It is not that programme, not about autoantibody assays at all, and holds no assay price, no assay sensitivity, no screening cost and no global figure. THREE CLASSES, the third new to this repo: (i) unit test prices it does not carry - $20/$22/$26/$10.50 per setting, the $5-50 range, the $20 HIC and $7 LMIC base cases; (ii) global screening-cost totals of $1B and $10B from a paper with no global figure, the same US-to-global error as 37909353; (iii) DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE claims - 82% base-case and 76-88% range GAD assay sensitivity - which are not cost claims, so no cost-provenance gate would ever have examined them. CONSEQUENCE: the LADA model now has NO sourced input of any kind. Base population unsourced 2026-09-10, insulin and complication costs unsourced 2026-09-13, test cost and test sensitivity unsourced today. Its only surviving citation is PMID:23248199 for the 9.7% prevalence rate, on the row that still carries [BASE MISMATCH]. The 2026-09-13 question of whether this model should publish at all is no longer a close one. AN ENTIRE UNAUDITED METHODOLOGY BLOCK FOUND IN A FILE ON NOBODY'S LIST: rebuild_clinical_trial_dashboard.py carried a 'Key References & Methodology' block in which FOUR OF FOUR citations were false - 29710129 labelled 'Zarin et al., N Engl J Med 2011' (it is Hernandez, JAMA Oncol 2018: wrong author, journal, decade and subject); 37909353 and 34763823 jointly labelled 'systematic reviews of the global trial pipeline' (a US cost-of-illness study and an insulin-pricing review, neither a systematic review); and 37105208 labelled 'IDF Atlas 10th ed.', which is THE SAME MISIDENTIFICATION WITH THE SAME LABEL repaired on the main Research Dashboard on 2026-09-10, recurring in a second file. Block withdrawn, method prose retained as uncited. The 2026-09-10 instruction to 'look for the rest of it' must NOT be closed on its named-file list. THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE FINDING IS CLINICAL, NOT ECONOMIC: build_islet_outcomes.py attributed 70% insulin independence at 10 years and 60% at 13.3 years under belatacept/efalizumab to 'Hering et al., PMID:37105208 (Lancet 2023)'. That PMID is Chetboun et al. (CITR Investigators), Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023;11(6):391-401, a retrospective registry cohort of 1210 patients on primary graft function with a FIVE-YEAR endpoint - wrong author, wrong journal title, not a costimulation-blockade study, and structurally incapable of reporting a 10-year or 13.3-year rate. The figures also contradict this same page, which gives 32% at 5 years and 20% at 10 years from CITR Annual Reports roughly sixty lines earlier: a 3.5x disagreement on the same outcome at the same timepoint on one page. Both attachments withdrawn and the figures marked DISPUTED rather than merely uncited, because unlike every other defect swept this month these are efficacy numbers a reader could act on. Not re-sourced, per the 2026-08-20 precedent. TWO CLEAN NEGATIVES WORTH RECORDING SO THEY ARE NOT RE-SWEPT: build_drug_repurposing_screen.py's 34 occurrences of 29710129 are ALL withdrawal records from the 2026-08-29 repair, not live claims - so the '~79 of 81 remaining' estimate was badly wrong, and the true live count was roughly a dozen; and build_immunomod_lada.py, build_drug_repurposing_islet.py and rebuild_website.py contain NO occurrences of 34763823 at all, though the 2026-09-13 item named all three as the sweep's remaining work. build_gka_pricing.py is materially swept: its three surviving attachments are insulin-price and correct-identity uses. NARROWED SELF-CONFESSED-DOUBT GATE RE-MEASURED as the 2026-09-12 item asked: 5 hits repo-wide, all in audit tooling, ZERO in builder-emitted HTML - confirming it is safe to wire and will find nothing. papers_contents_established.17065674: Li C, Ford ES, McGuire LC, Mokdad AH, Little RR, Reaven GM, 'Trends in Hyperinsulinemia Among Nondiabetic Adults in the U.S.', Diabetes Care 2006;29(11):2396-2402, doi 10.2337/dc06-0289. CDC. NHANES analysis comparing mean fasting serum insulin concentration and hyperinsulinemia prevalence among nondiabetic US adults between 1988-1994 and 1999-2002; concludes both rose markedly in parallel with the obesity epidemic. TEST: contains NO autoantibody assay price, NO assay sensitivity or specificity, NO screening cost, NO DASP workshop data and NO global figure. It is not a Diabetes Antibody Standardization Program report and has nothing to do with autoantibody testing. Any attachment to an assay cost, an assay performance characteristic, or a screening-programme cost is false by construction. Identity confirmed against the Diabetes Care journal listing, the PubMed record and the paper library index.
papers_contents_established.37105208: Chetboun M et al., Collaborative Islet Transplant Registry (CITR) Investigators, 'Association between primary graft function and 5-year outcomes of islet allogeneic transplantation in type 1 diabetes: a retrospective, multicentre, observational cohort study in 1210 patients from the Collaborative Islet Transplant Registry', Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023;11(6):391-401, doi 10.1016/S2213-8587(23)00082-7. Reports an inverse, independent, linear association between primary graft function measured 28 days after last islet infusion and the cumulative FIVE-YEAR incidence of unfavourable outcomes. TEST: the endpoint horizon is 5 years, so any attachment to a 10-year, 13.3-year or 20-year outcome is false by construction. It is not stratified by immunosuppression regimen and is not a study of belatacept, efalizumab or costimulation blockade. It is NOT the IDF Diabetes Atlas - that mislabel has now been found twice, in rebuild_research_dashboard.py (2026-09-10) and rebuild_clinical_trial_dashboard.py (2026-09-14). The first author is NOT Hering; that mislabel has been found twice in build_islet_outcomes.py. Journal is Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol, frequently abbreviated in this repo to 'Lancet 2023', which is itself wrong. First author graded LIKELY, not CERTAIN - read from the Mayo Clinic and Lancet listings, not round-tripped through eutils.

run_history.independent_verification: A verification pass was run over this run's own output before closing, and it found TWO real defects in the run's work plus one that overturned a conclusion. Recorded because the repo's standard is to show them. (1) THE RUN'S OWN CORRECTION WAS WRONG. Having withdrawn 'Hering et al., PMID:37105208' from the 70%-at-10-years belatacept figures in build_islet_outcomes.py, the run concluded 'no replacement source has been identified' and marked the numbers [UNSOURCED - DISPUTED]. That was false. The correct source, Voglova et al., 'A Multi-Modal Approach to Islet and Pancreas Transplantation With Calcineurin-Sparing Immunosuppression', Transpl Int 2023, PMID 37359825, doi 10.3389/ti.2023.11367, was ALREADY CITED CORRECTLY in the same file's Evidence Catalog about 700 lines below - a table the sweep never opened because it was grepping for the wrong PMID. The figures are real and correctly transcribed: 7 of 10 consecutive patients (4 efalizumab, 3 belatacept) insulin independent at 10 years, 6 of 10 at mean follow-up 13.3 +/- 1.1 years, 3 of the 7 having had a pancreas-after-islet transplant. Re-sourced, with the denominator now stated in visible text. LESSON, and it is the sharpest of the month: a citation sweep that asks only 'does this PMID support this claim' will mark correct numbers as unsupported. It must also ask 'where did this number actually come from', and the answer is often elsewhere in the same file. Withdrawing a true figure is not a safe failure - it destroys real evidence and it teaches the reader to distrust the disclosure markers. (2) A CLAIM SURVIVING WITHOUT ITS PMID. The sweep stripped PMID:17065674 from 21 places in build_lada_diagnostic_model.py but left the 'Key Assumptions' paragraph, which names the false source in WORDS - 'with 82% sensitivity (DASP workshops)' - and so was invisible to a PMID grep. Same for the '(DASP)' constant comments on GAD_TEST_SENSITIVITY and GAD_TEST_SPECIFICITY, the inline comment on the lada_detected calculation, and the Monte Carlo prior on gad_sensitivity in statistical_analysis.py. All now withdrawn. LOCATE THESE BY STRING, NOT LINE NUMBER: the round-2 edits shifted both files, and the line numbers this record originally carried were already stale by the end of the same run - which is itself a small lesson about writing line numbers into durable state. GENERALISABLE: strip the source NAME as well as the identifier, and add named-source strings to the sweep pattern. (3) TWO FURTHER LIVE ATTACHMENTS found in that same paragraph that three days of sweeps had missed: a $25 HIC test cost that contradicts the $20 used in two other tables in the same file, and a live PMID:37909353 attachment for a 'Medicare median ($5,876/year)' - withdrawn on the 2026-09-13 sweep's own stated finding that the paper contains no Medicare median. (4) UNRECONCILED AND QUEUED: GRAFT_DATA in build_islet_outcomes.py plots belatacept at 55% at year 10 while the prose on the same page says 70%. Flagged in place, not changed, because which is intended is a modelling decision. THE COMMON SHAPE OF ALL FOUR: every one was an error of SCOPE, not of content - the sweep was right about each PMID it examined and wrong about where to look. That is the third consecutive run in which verification found scope errors and no content errors.

new_defect_classes.sweep_withdrew_a_true_figure: The run withdrew a correct, correctly-transcribed clinical figure and declared it unsourced, because the wrong PMID was attached and the sweep never asked where the number really came from. The true source was elsewhere in the same file. This is the inverse of every other defect recorded this month and it is more damaging than leaving a bad citation in place, because it removes real evidence and devalues the [UNSOURCED] marker. MITIGATION, now standard: before marking a figure unsourced, grep the file for the figure ITSELF and for its subject matter, not only for the suspect PMID, and check any reference table or evidence catalog in the same file. If the number appears elsewhere with a different citation, the defect is a mis-attachment to be repaired, not a claim to be withdrawn.
new_defect_classes.claim_survives_pmid_removal: Stripping a PMID does not remove a provenance claim when the source is also named in prose. build_lada_diagnostic_model.py:685 continued to assert '82% sensitivity (DASP workshops)' after all 21 PMID attachments were withdrawn, and three code comments plus a Monte Carlo prior in a second file carried '(DASP)' as well. A PMID grep cannot see any of these. MITIGATION: for every concentration swept, add the source's NAME and any shorthand for it to the grep pattern - 'DASP', 'IDF Atlas', 'Cochrane', 'CMS', 'IQVIA', 'WHO model pricing', 'Medicare median' - and sweep the name and the identifier together.
new_defect_classes.state_record_wrong_driving_wrongful_with: A content record in agent_state.json was itself false, and the queue item built on it instructed a sweep that would have withdrawn correct citations. This is the first recorded instance of the agent's own memory, rather than the repository, being the defect. MITIGATION, now standard: before executing a sweep whose test rests on 'this paper contains nothing but X', re-verify X against a named retrieved source, and check whether the local abstract is a stub - a research Letter, Comment or Editorial will have a one-sentence PubMed descriptor from which no run can establish contents. Grade such records UNVERIFIED, not LIKELY.
new_defect_classes.same_outcome_two_values_one_page: build_islet_outcomes.py published 20% and 70% insulin independence at 10 years roughly sixty lines apart. This is the 2026-09-13 'one price, two values, one citation' test generalised from prices to CLINICAL OUTCOMES, and it needs no lookup: flag any page carrying the same outcome measure at the same timepoint with materially different values. Recommended as a gate; today's case is a known positive.
new_defect_classes.wrong_author_correct_pmid: PMID 37105208 was attributed to 'Hering et al.' in two places and 29710129 to 'Zarin et al.' in one. The PMID resolves, the title may not even be asserted, and audit_prose_citation_titles.py checks titles rather than author surnames - so an author-name assertion is currently unchecked anywhere in the pipeline. Cheap gate: for every prose citation that names an author surname, compare it against the paper library's authors field. That field is already populated in the abstracts JSON.

papers_contents_established.29710129: [CONTENT RECORD CORRECTED 2026-09-14 - THE FIGURES RECORDED HERE ON 2026-09-13 WERE WRONG AND WOULD HAVE CAUSED A WRONGFUL MASS WITHDRAWAL. Retained verbatim for the audit trail, then corrected.] ORIGINAL TEXT: 'Hernandez, Prasad & Gellad, Total Costs of Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Immunotherapy, JAMA Oncol 2018;4(7):994-996. Research letter. Total CAR-T cost at least $750,000; non-drug costs $400,000-450,000, roughly equal to drug costs. TEST: any attachment to a non-CAR-T cost is false by construction.' CORRECTION: the bibliographic identity is right and the topic test is right, but BOTH dollar figures are wrong and the drug/non-drug split was inverted. ACTUAL CONTENTS, confirmed 2026-09-14 from the Healio report of the research letter and a second independent summary, both naming Hernandez directly: list prices ARE stated in the paper - tisagenlecleucel $475,000 and axicabtagene ciloleucel $373,000. Mean total expected cost $510,963 for tisagenlecleucel (range $478,777 without CRS to $531,813 with CRS; $432,131 after Novartis outcomes-based pricing) and $402,647 for axicabtagene ciloleucel. NON-DRUG COSTS ARE 7% OF TOTAL - about $30,000-$36,000 for the average patient and up to $56,000-$60,000 with severe cytokine release syndrome. NOT $400,000-450,000. Method: 11 patient-treatment pathways weighted by probability, using 2017 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, OPPS, Part B payment limits and HCUP estimates, with probabilities from FDA documents and the ELIANA trial. Budget impact: 600 eligible tisagenlecleucel patients/year = $259 million; 7,500 eligible axicabtagene patients/year = $3 billion. Explicitly NOT a cost-effectiveness analysis - no ICER, no QALY. WHY THE ERROR MATTERED: the 2026-09-13 record asserted the paper holds no drug price, which made the ten $475K/$373K attachments in build_cart_access.py look false. They are CORRECT and were retained. The $750,000 figure appears nowhere in this paper; it most likely came from the 'Accounting for All Costs' correspondence (PMID 30325998) arguing Hernandez UNDERestimated, which is a different document. CORRECTED TESTS: (a) any attachment to a non-CAR-T cost remains false by construction - unchanged; (b) any attachment of a non-drug or CRS-management cost ABOVE roughly $60,000 to this paper is false; (c) the $475K/$373K list prices and the $510,963/$402,647 totals ARE supported and must not be withdrawn; (d) any attachment to a diabetes figure, an ICER or a QALY is false. LESSON: the local abstract file for this PMID is a one-sentence stub because the paper is a research Letter, so no run can establish its contents from the paper library - the 2026-09-13 run recorded specific dollar figures it could not have read, and graded itself LIKELY. A content record that cannot be traced to a named retrieved source should be graded UNVERIFIED, not LIKELY.

Fri 2026-08-21 - THE TOP-RANKED RESEARCH PATH ON THE SITE HAD NO EVIDENCE BEHIND IT. (1) ONE ROOT CAUSE, NOT TWO. The bilingual double-count and the table-fragment defect logged 2026-08-18 are the same bug: section types FIG, TABLE and ABBR were documented as skip-worthy in the source comment since the file was written but were never added to SKIP_SECTION_TYPES. PMID 39412512 carries its results table twice (English section 60, Portuguese section 247, both typed TABLE) - that is where "10 mg or"/"10 mg ou" came from. Measured both options rather than assuming: scanning TABLE yields 58 extra extractions, and all 58 were inspected individually - 46 bare dose labels, 7 abbreviation glossaries, 5 table cross-references, zero measurements. TABLE stays skipped. (2) THE LARGER DEFECT, found while proving the fix. inflammatory_markers patterns ended in an unbounded `.*?(\d+)`, so the capture took the first digit downstream regardless of distance, sentence boundary or unit. 85 of 92 extractions were not measurements: the 3 in NLRP3, the 1 in IL-1, the year 2014, section number 7.2, sample size 500. Patterns rewritten to require a sentence-bounded gap plus a unit, a direction-verb-tied percent, or a fold change: 92 -> 7, and all 7 survivors carry an explicit unit. Corpus 414 -> 292. (3) THE CASUALTIES. Recounted all 47 paths against live extraction; 29 are HOLLOW with exactly zero surviving data points. Worst is NLRP3_inflammasome -> inflammation, formerly rank #1 with 61 data points, whose displayed key_claims were prose fragments like "NLRP3 activation could be a trigger for DKD. Additionally, pharmacological inhibition of the IL-1" with "value" = 1. Its two sources are both narrative reviews. (4) SUPPRESSION LEAKED THREE MORE TIMES. Removing hollow paths from the path dashboard left them live in the validated-path store (different key spelling), in the validation_summary counter (read from a precomputed field, never recomputed - page rendered "Total paths: 17" beside "VALIDATED paths (22 total)"), and in the Bayesian ranking, which was still publishing oxidative_stress -> inflammation at posterior 72.7% MODERATE and NLRP3_inflammasome -> inflammation at 55.3% - both with zero evidence. Sat 2026-08-22 - FIVE MORE EXTRACTORS WERE MAJORITY ARTIFACT, AND THE EXTRACTION STEP WAS NOT IN THE PIPELINE. (1) THE MEASUREMENT. The P1 item flagged c_peptide, hba1c_change, survival_graft and remission as suspect BY CONSTRUCTION. All four were, and so was autoantibody, which the item did not list: survival_graft 6/6 artifact, c_peptide 5/5, remission 34/48, autoantibody 3/5, hba1c_change 5/10. Corpus artifact rate 18.2%. The control that makes this credible: inflammatory_markers, rewritten the day before, scored 0% under the identical signature set. (2) WHAT THEY WERE PUBLISHING. "insulin independence was 45.5 +/- 32.0 months" became a 7.1% graft survival figure. "glycated hemoglobin level and insulin dose. RESULTS At 1 year, the mean AUC for the level of C peptide..." became an HbA1c of 6.76. The trial registration CTRI/2020/08/027072 became a remission denominator. (3) THE FIX. Every gap bounded to [^.\n]{0,N}?, every capture required to carry a unit, a percent sign or an explicit denominator - the same three rules applied to inflammatory_markers on 2026-08-21. Plus five new rejection reasons: IDENTIFIER_FRACTION, IMPLAUSIBLE_FRACTION, DEFINITION_THRESHOLD, PROJECTED_NOT_MEASURED, ATTRIBUTED_TO_OTHER_STUDY. Corpus 292 -> 240; artifact rate 18.2% -> 0.0%. (4) PROVENANCE, A NEW DEFECT CLASS. PMID 36643381 is a colchicine trial PROTOCOL. It was supplying two inflammatory-marker data points: one from "we estimated that hs-CRP is suppressed to 3.22 mg/L" - a sample-size assumption for a trial that had not run - and one from "the previous report indicating that colchicine 1 mg for 4 weeks reduced hs-CRP by about 60%", which is somebody else's result. A projection served as a measurement is the worst error this repo can make. (5) THE BIGGER ONE, FOUND SIDEWAYS. Building the design-paper gate revealed that PMID 39613428 - titled "...protocol for a randomised, double-blind ... trial" - is the SOLE corpus source for both `verapamil -> beta_cell` and `verapamil -> T1D`, the #2 and #3 paths on the dashboard, and contributes nothing but planned doses. Escalated as a human call rather than delisted unattended. (6) THE STRUCTURAL FINDING. extract_corpus_data.py was never in run_quality_improvements.py. Four dashboards and the landing page read its output, so the runner could report 47/47 green over arbitrarily stale extraction - and did: the 2026-08-21 extractor fix had not reached PMID 32862232 until this run re-ran it by hand. Now step 33 of 50. Two new gates registered alongside it (audit_extractor_wildcards.py, audit_baseline_citations.py); the wildcard gate was negative-tested by reinjecting the historical remission pattern, which it caught along with all 23 artifacts it reproduced. run_history.summary: THE AUTHOR-SURNAME GATE WAS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST MEASUREMENT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RESULT OF THE DAY - NOT THE DEFECTS IT FOUND, BUT THE DEFECTS IT NEARLY INVENTED. Specified as the 2026-09-14 queue item described it ('for every builder occurrence of <Surname> et al. within ~80 characters of a PMID, compare against authors[0]'), the gate reported 103 mismatches. Inspection of the source showed essentially ALL of them were correctly cited. The cause: this repo writes semicolon-separated citation runs ('Hoppe et al. ... (PMID:28010783); Zhang et al. ... (PMID:36109742); Clemens et al. ... (PMID:32312859)'), and a SYMMETRIC window centred on a surname reaches BACKWARDS and matches the PREVIOUS citation's PMID first. Every surname in a list was therefore tested against its predecessor, producing a perfect shift-by-one chain of fake mismatches. Had the gate shipped as specified it would have driven mass 'correction' of correct citations - the exact inverse of its purpose. FOUR false-positive classes were found and fixed: (i) reverse window straddle, fixed by forward-only pairing that stops at a separator or an intervening 'et al.'; (ii) PubMed initials captured as the surname ('Khan MAB et al.' -> 'MAB'), 22 hits; (iii) slash-joined author runs ('Reichman/Markmann/Odorico et al.') where the LAST name was captured instead of the first; (iv) HTML-entity and diacritic folding ('Abramoff' vs 'Abràmoff', 'Stenstrom' vs 'Stenström'). After those fixes: 171 attributions checked, 151 confirmed CORRECT, 20 flagged. The gate also reproduced the known-positive test set (Zarin/29710129, Hering/37105208), so its reach is real and not an artifact of loosening. EIGHT FALSE CITATIONS WERE THEN FIXED across five builders, each verified against NCBI esummary, and the pattern in them is worse than a wrong surname: in four cases the cited PMID is a paper on an unrelated subject. 10919952 (asserted 'Shapiro, NEJM 2000', islet transplantation) is Zeisel, 'Is there a metabolic basis for dietary supplementation?', Am J Clin Nutr - repointed to 10911004, and note it occurred TWICE, the second instance inside a JS onclick handler where no prose gate could see it. 17596481 (asserted 'Balk, chromium') is Metzger, the Fifth Workshop-Conference GESTATIONAL DIABETES guideline - repointed to 17519436, also two instances. 12122111 (asserted 'Hundal, salsalate') is Chaisson, a mouse hepatocyte NF-kB study - repointed to 12021247, and the drug name was corrected too because Hundal 2002 studied ASPIRIN, not salsalate. 24838679 (asserted 'Antvorskov, dietary gluten') is Galderisi, a single-author Comment - repointed to 24871322. 32943753 (asserted 'Hu, Nature 2020, gasdermin D') is Agrawal, a podocyte review in Nat Rev Nephrol 2021 - WITHDRAWN, no replacement located. 18073361 (asserted 'UKPDS' for a GADA prevalence figure) is Willi, 'Active smoking and the risk of type 2 diabetes', JAMA 2007 - WITHDRAWN twice, no replacement located. DISCIPLINE NOTE: a candidate replacement for the berberine trial (18191047) was checked and REJECTED - it is Alemzadeh on hypovitaminosis D - so that surname was dropped rather than guessed. Replacements were asserted ONLY where esummary confirmed both title and journal.

On 2026-09-14 this agent corrected a false attribution on the belatacept 10-year figures, re-sourced them to PMID 37359825, verified the paper's CONTENTS against its abstract, and recorded in agent_state.json: '37359825: Voglova et al., Transpl Int 2023. Voglova is not an author on it; Voglova's islet papers are 33599904 and 28632818, different work. Then it wrote that inheritance into memory as verified, which would have made every later sweep skip it. Five occurrences, one of them the clickable Evidence Catalog row. TWO STRUCTURAL CAUSES, BOTH NOW CLOSED. (1) The surname gate's UNKNOWN bucket was not neutral. It declines to flag a PMID absent from the local paper library, which is defensible, except that a PMID is missing from the library exactly when it was added recently and by hand - which is also when it is most likely to be wrong. 'Unknown' was concentrated on the riskiest citations in the repo. --resolve-unknown now resolves that bucket against NCBI esummary with an on-disk cache: 16 of 16 resolved, 0 unresolvable, and it is opt-in so a network blip cannot fail the build. (2) Identifiers inside markup were unreachable. --html now scans generated .html for <a> elements whose PMID sits in an attribute with the surname in the anchor text - the class where the Shapiro/10919952 defect survived a full sweep on 2026-09-15 and was caught only by an ad-hoc grep. run_history.summary: THE HUB PUBLISHED TWO DRUG-SPECIFIC SUCCESS RATES THAT ITS SOURCE NEVER REPORTED, AND IT BUILT THEM OUT OF ONE COHORT MEASURED TWICE. Wisel et al., Transpl Int 2023 (PMID 37359825) is ten consecutive T1D islet recipients, five on belatacept and five on efalizumab. Its abstract says 70% (four EFA, three BELA) were insulin independent at 10 years and 60% at mean follow-up 13.3 years -- the same ten people, twice. build_gap_deep_dives.py published 'Belatacept 70% at 10yr, Efalizumab 60% at 13.3yr', which converts a difference of TIMEPOINT into a difference of DRUG, manufactures two per-drug rates that do not exist in the paper, and assigns belatacept the better number when efalizumab in fact contributed MORE of the seven responders (four versus three). The same invention appeared a second time in clinical_pipeline. A third error in the same file pinned the 13.3-year numerator to the 10-year endpoint ('6/10 insulin-independent at 10 years'), so the file simultaneously published 70%-at-10-years and 6/10-at-10-years for one paper, 34 lines apart. A fourth line promised a 'Belatacept comparative efficacy' study that does not exist: the paper the hub relies on has no comparator arm at all. Also unstated anywhere: three of the seven ten-year successes got there via PANCREAS-after-islet transplant and are therefore back on a calcineurin inhibitor -- in a field whose entire claim is calcineurin-sparing. WHY EIGHTY-ODD GREEN GATES SAW NONE OF IT: every gate in this repository scores ONE assertion against ONE source. 37359825 is a real PMID, correctly titled, correctly attributed to Wisel, genuinely about belatacept and islet transplant -- it passes the identifier gate, the title gate, the surname gate, the subject gate and the trial-phase gate individually. A contradiction is not a property of any single claim, so no quantity of per-claim gates can ever see one. build_islet_outcomes.py had carried the CORRECT pooled reading, with denominators, since 2026-09-14. The repository held the right answer and the invented one at the same time, in two files, both green. THE NEW GATE'S FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND WAS THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF OF THIS RUN. Version one associated a value with the sole PMID within 900 characters. Its first measurement reported a conflict: PMID 40544428 at one year holding 61%, 61%, 67%. That is not a defect -- 61% is Edmonton and 67% is LANTIDRA, two different cohorts correctly having different one-year rates near one citation. The gate had manufactured a contradiction out of proximity, which is exactly the failure its own docstring claimed to have made impossible, and exactly what the 2026-09-15 surname gate (103 reported, nearly all invented) and the 2026-09-18 coordinate gate had already taught. Rewritten so attribution is EXPLICIT ONLY: a value belongs to an identifier when the author wrote them in the same statement. Nothing is inferred from distance. THAT HONESTY COST THE GATE ITS GRIP ON THE DEFECT THAT MOTIVATED IT, AND MEASURING WHY IS THE REAL FINDING. Under the strict rule the conflict check is silent on 37359825, because only one statement about it carries a PMID. So: 46 endpoint-values exist across builder source, and THREE carry a citation in the same statement. Thirty-five carry none. 'Belatacept 70% at 10yr' was never mis-cited -- it was never cited, and neither is almost any clinical percentage this hub publishes. A reader meets a number with no source, no denominator and no cohort, and it looks authoritative only because of the company it keeps. The gate ships with a ratchet on that count: it may fall, it must never rise, so a new uncited clinical percentage now fails the build the day it is added. The conflict half is dormant by construction and becomes load-bearing only as the ratchet drives the backlog down. NINE P0 ITEMS WERE ONE REAL PROBLEM AND EIGHT RESTATEMENTS OF TWO DEAD ONES. run_history.second_pass: THE FIRST PASS OF THIS RUN CLAIMED TO HAVE FIXED THE BELATACEPT FABRICATION AND HAD FIXED ONE INSTANCE OF IT IN ONE FILE. An adversarial re-check of that claim -- run specifically to try to falsify it rather than confirm it -- found the same invented figure live in FOUR builders and in both published dashboard copies. build_gap_deep_dives.py line 278, twenty lines below a correction the first pass had just written, read 'CTLA-4 Ig (belatacept): 70% graft survival at 10yr vs 32% with tacrolimus'. build_data_dictionary.py carried it twice with a 50% comparator, cited to PMID:16120857. build_gap_synthesis.py carried it with no comparator and no citation. THREE FILES, THREE DIFFERENT TACROLIMUS COMPARATORS (32%, 50%, none) FOR ONE NUMBER, which is by itself sufficient evidence that the number was never read off a paper. PMID 16120857 was fetched live this run: Vincenti et al., NEJM 2005, a RENAL transplant trial whose comparator is CYCLOSPORINE, not tacrolimus, with endpoints of acute rejection at SIX MONTHS and GFR at TWELVE MONTHS. It contains no ten-year endpoint, no graft-survival percentage, no 70 and no 50. A fourth conflation runs through all of it: GRAFT SURVIVAL is not INSULIN INDEPENDENCE. The only long-term figure this hub legitimately holds is 7-of-10 insulin independence (PMID:37359825) -- a different outcome, a different population, and n=10. All four sites are now corrected and re-verified absent from source and from both published copies. THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE FIRST PASS'S METHOD, NOT ITS LUCK. It found the defect by reading one paper against one file, then verified its repair by grepping for THE STRINGS IT HAD JUST EDITED. That test can only ever confirm the edit; it cannot find a fifth copy, because a grep for text you wrote is a grep for your own memory. The search that worked was the one that started from the CLAIM ('belatacept, 70%, ten years') and swept the whole corpus for anything asserting it. Verify the claim, not the edit. THE NEW GATE WAS ALSO WRONG IN TWO WAYS, BOTH FOUND BY THE SAME RE-CHECK AND BOTH NOW FIXED. (1) IT COULD NOT FAIL A BUILD. main() computed status='FAIL' and then returned 0 unconditionally, while run_quality_improvements.py dispatches on the return code. Every claim the first pass made about this gate 'failing the build the day a new uncited percentage is added' was therefore false as shipped -- a gate that reports and calls itself a gate is worse than no gate, because the green line is now evidence of nothing while looking like evidence of something. (2) IT HAD REAL FALSE POSITIVES: it keys on (identifier, timepoint) and never parses WHAT IS MEASURED, so '61% at 5 years in adults' versus '32% at 5 years in children', and 'insulin independence 44% at 1 year' versus 'C-peptide positivity 90% at 1 year', both registered as contradictions. Both are correct writing. An outcome-word filter and an explicit closed list of cohort-partition words now suppress both classes, re-proven on fixtures. But a heuristic that works most of the time must not be allowed to fail a build -- that is the 2026-09-15 surname mistake and the 2026-09-18 coordinate mistake, and this repository has now made some version of it three times, twice in this single run. So the split is explicit: the RATCHET fails (purely mechanical -- an identifier is on the line or it is not), the CONFLICT check only reports and a human adjudicates. Ratchet moved 35 -> 31 as the corrections added citations.

The chart now plots the paper's two reported timepoints as hollow markers with no connecting line, because nothing was measured between them. A fifth 10-year figure ('~70% ... modeled trajectory') and the claim that 'belatacept recipients maintain superior graft function throughout follow-up' were withdrawn in the same pass -- the source's only per-drug number points the other way, four of seven responders being on efalizumab.

findings: EASD Vienna 2025 (Sep 15-19) presentation + broad trade coverage: benefit does not survive withdrawal. C-peptide significantly higher at week 72, NO LONGER significant at week 96.
Reported means: 72w 0.49 (baricitinib) vs 0.36 (placebo); 96w 0.37 vs 0.26. Treatment was 48 weeks, follow-up 96 weeks from treatment start, n=91, ages 10-30, within 100 days of diagnosis.

bandit_96week_2026_09.why_it_matters: The repo carries baricitinib as an active repurposing signal. dapan_dia_2026_09.topic: DAPAN-DIA NCT06047262 dapansutrile T2D primary results
findings: Still enrolling. Design per AHA 2024 abstract 4115645 (Circulation 150 suppl 1): n=300, T2D with HbA1c >7.5% and hsCRP >1.5 mg/L, dapansutrile 1000 mg BID vs placebo 2:1, 6 months, primary endpoint change in HbA1c; secondaries IL-1beta, IL-6, hsCRP, MASLD progression.
Described as the first adequately-powered placebo-controlled trial of an oral NLRP3-specific inhibitor. Estimated completion 2026.
dapan_dia_2026_09.why_it_matters: This is the trial that would move SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD off surrogate biomarkers - except it will not: the primary endpoint is HbA1c, and the secondaries are inflammatory biomarkers. Even a positive DAPAN-DIA does NOT supply the renal hard endpoint the P4 queue item has been waiting for since 2026-08-17. Recording that now so a future run does not mistake this readout for gap closure.

No peer-reviewed publication of extension results located.
Adjacent and NEW: NCT07360080 "Long-Term Outcomes of Teplizumab in Routine Clinical Care" - registry-style real-world study. UNVERIFIED identifier, queued for registry confirmation.

Dapagliflozin alone reduces systemic inflammation in T2D (Cardiovascular Diabetology 2024, PMID 38849829 / PMC11161924): 12-month RCT found reductions in IL-1β and CRP vs placebo, with correlated GLS improvement.

Colchicine alone: COLCOT-T2D (colcot-t2d.org) is an ongoing RCT evaluating low-dose colchicine 0.5 mg/day for CV event reduction in T2D without known CVD. Primary endpoint is cardiovascular, not metabolic.
No published RCT (PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov as of April 2026) combines dapagliflozin + colchicine in diabetes.
Mechanistic rationale exists (both reduce NLRP3-inflammasome signalling via independent routes — SGLT2 inhibition and tubulin polymerisation respectively) but has not been prospectively tested.
dapagliflozin_plus_colchicine_diabetes.recommendation: Do not list dapagliflozin+colchicine as an evidence-backed combination on any dashboard. If discussed, label 'MECHANISTIC HYPOTHESIS — no combination RCT evidence'.

tegoprubart_islet_t1d.finding: ATTD Barcelona March 2026 data (12 patients, UChicago) remains conference-presented only; no peer-reviewed journal publication located.
