BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.mechanism: β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome assembly by blocking K+ efflux and ASC oligomerization; independent of UCP2/Sirt2/Gpr109a/HDAC. SGLT2i raise serum BHB, providing a candidate mechanistic link to NLRP3 suppression in DKD/CV outcomes.

external_pmids.25686106: Youm et al. Nat Med 2015 — foundational: BHB blocks NLRP3-mediated disease (cell+mouse).
external_pmids.28794421: Yamanashi et al. Sci Rep 2017 — BHB endogenic NLRP3 inhibitor; anti-inflammatory in stress model.
external_pmids.32358544: Kim et al. Nat Commun 2020 — SGLT2i in T2D+CVD pts: ↑BHB, ↓insulin, ↓NLRP3-IL-1β in human macrophages (30-day RCT vs SU).
external_pmids.34918381: Front Pharmacol/Ke 2022 — already in library; SGLT2i↔NLRP3 via itaconate (alternate axis).
external_pmids.39412512: Braz J Nephrol 2024 — SGLT2i+NLRP3 in DKD review (already in library).
external_pmids.40055596: BMC Nephrology 2025 review (Li et al; s12882-025-04019-0) - KD/BHB delays DKD progression via anti-inflammation (incl. NLRP3), anti-oxidative-stress, anti-fibrosis, autophagy. Captures the previously-uncaptured 2025 BMC Nephrology source.
external_pmids.40793083: Liu et al, J Diabetes 2025 (PMC12340978) - MULTI-COHORT (NHANES cross-sectional + West China T2DM-DKD longitudinal Cox/RCS + Mendelian randomization): elevated circulating beta-OHB INDEPENDENTLY associated with REDUCED ESRD risk (nonlinear; high-normal BHB may delay DKD progression). First human hard-renal-outcome + MR support for the BHB->renal-protection link.

caveats: Most BHB→NLRP3 evidence is in vitro / mouse models. The in-human Kim 2020 study is a pharmacodynamic biomarker readout, not a clinical-outcome RCT.
BHB rise from SGLT2i is modest (typically 0.1–0.5 mmol/L) — whether this magnitude is sufficient to produce clinically meaningful NLRP3 inhibition in humans remains unproven.
2025 BMC Nephrology review (Springer; PMID not yet captured) and 2025 ADA abstract 389-P (BHB mitigates DKD) are non-PMID/abstract-only sources, so weight cautiously.
Alternative mechanisms (itaconate, RIP1-RIP3-MLKL, TXNIP-NLRP3) ALSO proposed for SGLT2i — BHB is not the sole or proven dominant axis.

2025 mechanistic PREPRINT (bioRxiv 2025.05.01.650510, Univ Vermont; NOT peer-reviewed, NO PMID - weight cautiously): NLRP3 inhibition is manifested only by the ACID form (beta-hydroxybutyric acid) or in an acidic microenvironment; sodium-BHB and NaOH-neutralized BHBA do NOT inhibit NLRP3. Implication: modest, physiological-pH serum BHB elevations from SGLT2i may be insufficient to engage NLRP3 - tempers the linear SGLT2i->BHB->NLRP3 translation story (mechanistic linearity DOWN even as human outcome association is UP).
BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.recommendation: Add an explicit "BHB→NLRP3" path entry in research_paths.json next pipeline rebuild; flag SGLT2i→NLRP3 as having multiple proposed mechanisms (BHB, itaconate, TXNIP-NLRP3) rather than a single linear story.
BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.reaffirm_note_2026-07-07: REAFFIRMED VALIDATED (preclinical HIGH; clinical MEDIUM, unchanged). Web sweep 2026-07-07 added 2 peer-reviewed 2025 PMIDs: 40055596 (BMC Nephrol review) and 40793083 (J Diabetes multi-cohort+MR: higher BHB -> lower ESRD risk in DKD). Human OUTCOME association strengthened. Offsetting: bioRxiv acidosis-licensing preprint suggests only acid-form/low-pH BHB inhibits NLRP3, questioning whether modest neutral-pH SGLT2i-driven BHB rise engages NLRP3 - so NLRP3 is likely not the sole/linear axis. Net: no tier change, no clinical promotion; mechanism reaffirmed but SGLT2i->NLRP3 remains multi-mechanism (BHB/itaconate/TXNIP) and BHB engagement is form/pH-conditional.

TXNIP_NLRP3_beta_cell_DKD.mechanism: High glucose drives ROS, TXNIP dissociates from thioredoxin and binds NLRP3, triggering inflammasome assembly and IL-1beta. Operates in BOTH pancreatic beta cells (pyroptosis) and renal mesangial/podocyte cells (DKD), a shared TXNIP/NLRP3 axis.

external_evidence.Shah 2016 (PMC4736396): High glucose + LPS prime ROS/TXNIP/NLRP3/IL-1beta in mesangial cells (DKD).
external_evidence.PMC5102753: TXNIP mediates NLRP3 activation, susceptibility to ischemic AKI in diabetes.
external_evidence.PMC8645844: miR-17-5p inhibits TXNIP/NLRP3, suppresses beta-cell pyroptosis in diabetic mice.
external_evidence.Canagliflozin 2025 (10.1007/s10753-025-0: SGLT2i attenuates podocyte injury via suppressing TXNIP/NLRP3 in DKD mice (drug-tractable).
external_evidence.NLRP3 pyroptosis DKD SR 2025 (PMC1220641: Systematic review: NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis in diabetic nephropathy — pathogenic mechanisms & therapeutic targets; reaffirms TXNIP as upstream redox-dependent NLRP3 activator in renal cells. Still mechanistic/preclinical; no human RCT on TXNIP/NLRP3 endpoints.
external_evidence.TIX100 / TiximED Phase 1 (2025-2026): First direct small-molecule TXNIP-TRX complex inhibitor to reach humans. Phase 1 SAD in healthy volunteers: well tolerated, no clinically significant safety findings; MAD Phase 1b funded (+$2.2M PRI) for T1D. Moves the TXNIP/NLRP3 axis from purely preclinical toward drug-tractable in humans, but NO efficacy RCT on TXNIP/NLRP3 or glycemic endpoints yet. Sources: Managed Healthcare Executive; Pharmacy Times; tiximed.com/news; Frontiers Endocrinol 2024 (10.3389/fendo.2024.1476444). Note: verapamil remains the only indirect TXNIP-lowering agent with human beta-cell efficacy data (and adult Ver-A-T1D primary was equivocal).
external_evidence.Zhang 2025 CHOP-TXNIP (PMID 40020889): UPR-activated NLRP3 drives pyroptotic+apoptotic podocyte injury via CHOP-TXNIP axis in DKD (confirms shared axis, drug-tractable). Neurochem Int 2025.
external_evidence.EGCG DKD (PMC11666909): Epigallocatechin-3-gallate ameliorates DKD by inhibiting TXNIP/NLRP3/IL-1beta (2nd independent DKD confirming source).
external_evidence.NLRP3 in diabetes review (PMC12395217, 2: Systematic review unifies mitochondrial-oxidative-stress->TXNIP->NLRP3 across beta cells + complications.

verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.path_name: Verapamil -> TXNIP suppression -> beta cell preservation (T1D)
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.rationale: Two independent RCTs confirm sustained C-peptide preservation. Ovalle 2018 (Nat Med, NCT02372253, n=24 completers, adults) showed verapamil improved MMTT-stimulated C-peptide AUC at both 3 and 12 months (prespecified primary endpoint), with lower insulin requirement increase and fewer hypoglycemic events. Forlenza CLVer trial 2023 (JAMA, n=88 pediatric ages 7-17) showed C-peptide 30% higher at 52 weeks vs placebo, with 95% vs 71% retaining peak C-peptide >=0.2 pmol/mL. Both trials used similar dosing and endpoint timing. Mechanism (TXNIP suppression) consistent with preclinical literature. AEs comparable to placebo.
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.caveats: Both trials are short-term (12 months). The 2022 follow-up exploratory work (Nat Commun, Ovalle group) showed broader systemic effects but did not establish durability beyond 1 year. Ver-A-T1D protocol (PMC11605811) is a multicenter RCT still enrolling - longer-term durability and any disease-modification beyond C-peptide preservation remain open.
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.revisit_2026_07_09: DOWNGRADED VALIDATED->PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Ver-A-T1D (Pieber/Graz; n=136 adults, 21 sites, 6 EU countries; recruitment completed May 2024), the largest and most rigorous independent ADULT replication, reported a NEUTRAL primary at EASD 2025 (Vienna, Sep 2025): NO significant C-peptide (AUC) difference vs placebo at 12 months in ITT, and no difference at 3/6/9 months. This directly contradicts the positive adult signal from the smaller Ovalle 2018 trial (n=24 completers, PMID 29988125). The pediatric CLVer RCT (Forlenza JAMA 2023, n=88, PMID 36826844) remains positive at 52 weeks, and the TXNIP/L-type-Ca-channel mechanism is robust in preclinical work. Net: mechanism sound; pediatric preservation replicated; adult efficacy now UNCERTAIN after a well-powered negative primary. 2-yr AUC and an open-label extension (>3yr) are planned for Ver-A-T1D. As of Jul 2026 the EASD result appears conference-presented; peer-reviewed full publication not yet confirmed.

external_refs_2026.EASD2025_Ver-A-T1D: Pieber et al., Ver-A-T1D primary results presented EASD 2025 (news-medical 20250918; healio 20250924) - neutral 12-mo C-peptide.

rituximab -> T1D.evidence: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): RCT n=87, 4-dose rituximab vs placebo in newly diagnosed T1D. At 1 year, rituximab group had significantly higher C-peptide AUC, lower HbA1c, lower insulin requirements vs placebo. 2-year extension Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline became parallel to placebo after ~8.2-month delay; effect transient. Conclusion: rituximab DELAYS but does not arrest beta-cell loss in recent-onset T1D. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED — real but limited durable benefit.
rituximab -> T1D.caveat: Effect plateaus by 30 months; no evidence of disease modification beyond delayed C-peptide loss. Underlying autoimmunity not arrested.

external_evidence_2026.2025_network_MA (PMC12211534, Diabetolog: Network MA of immunomodulatory RCTs in new-onset T1D; rituximab among agents reducing C-peptide loss vs placebo - confirms transient/partial beta-cell preservation.
external_evidence_2026.2025_BMC_Endocr_Disord (s12902-025-02088: SR/MA finds paradoxical dissociation between beta-cell preservation and glycemic control across immunomodulators incl. rituximab - reinforces PARTIALLY (real C-peptide effect, limited durable clinical benefit).

rituximab -> T1D.reaffirm_note_2026-06-24: REAFFIRMED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Two independent 2025 SR/MA now externally corroborate the transient/partial effect; no change in tier.
rituximab -> T1D.revisit_note: 2026-07-14 reaffirmed PARTIAL: Rituximab delays C-peptide decline ~8.2 mo at 1 yr (NEJM 2009 PMID 19940299) and effect persists to 2 yr (Diabetes Care 2014 PMID 24026563 / PMC6410357), but extended follow-up shows benefit disappears by ~30 mo (decline parallels placebo) — B-cell depletion alone does not alter underlying pathophysiology. No net-new RCT/SR since last check. Rating unchanged.
rituximab -> T1D.reaffirm_note: 2026-07-29: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED reaffirmed & strengthened. 2025 systematic review + network meta-analysis (PMC12211534; 60 RCTs, 4597 pts, 32 intervention classes, searches to 2024-07-31) confirms rituximab partially preserves 1-yr C-peptide but ranks below low-dose ATG/teplizumab; benefit transient (~8.2-mo delay in decline, parallels placebo by 30 mo). NEW: NCT07041268 (2025) testing REPEATED rituximab courses in adolescents — directly probes whether re-dosing addresses the known transience. No evidence yet of durable disease modification. Status unchanged: real but limited durable benefit.

rituximab -> beta_cell.key_finding: Rituximab transiently preserves C-peptide (~8 mo delay in decline at 1-2 yr) but effect wanes; B-cell depletion alone insufficient to arrest beta-cell loss.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_note: Reaffirmed by 2 fresh 2025 syntheses: BMC Medicine network meta-analysis (10.1186/s12916-025-04201-z) ranks low-dose ATG & teplizumab ABOVE rituximab for 1-2yr C-peptide preservation; BMC Endocrine Disorders SR/MA (10.1186/s12902-025-02088-8, PMC12636228) shows 'paradoxical dissociation' between beta-cell preservation and glycemic control across immunomodulators. Rituximab effect modest & transient, wanes after 1yr. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_06_22: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Web sweep returned only pre-2026 evidence: NEJMoa0904452 (PMID 19940299, 1-yr partial preservation), Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr results (PMID 24026563) showing 8.2-mo delay in C-peptide decline that then parallels placebo. Comparative MA still ranks rituximab BELOW low-dose ATG & teplizumab. No new 2026 RCT/MA. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_note_2026_07_04: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. 2025 BMC Medicine network meta-analysis (PMC12211534 / doi 10.1186/s12916-025-04201-z; 60 RCTs, 4597 pts, lit through 2024-07-31) reports 11 interventions with significantly higher 12-mo C-peptide than placebo - rituximab/anti-CD20 is NOT among them; anti-CD20 effect described as transient (patients eventually progress). Landmark Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMC6410357) positive at 1yr but wanes. No upgrade - effect modest/transient, does not arrest beta-cell loss.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_07_23: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (Thu run). Web sweep: 12-mo C-peptide preservation confirmed (Pescovitz NEJM 2009, PMID 19940299); effect transient - Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr results (PMID 24026563) show ~8.2-mo delay then decline parallels placebo as CD19+ B-cells recover (~69% baseline by 1yr). 2025 network MA (PMC12211534) lists 11 interventions beating placebo at 12-mo C-peptide; anti-CD20/rituximab NOT among top performers (teplizumab, baricitinib, cyclosporin lead). No new 2026 rituximab RCT/MA. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_08_12: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (Wed run). Fresh web sweep: no new completed 2026 rituximab RCT/MA. Core evidence unchanged - Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299, NEJMoa0904452/PMC6410357) partial 12-mo C-peptide preservation; 2-yr wane (PMID 24026563); 2025 network MA PMC12211534 (60 RCTs) still excludes anti-CD20/rituximab from the 11 interventions beating placebo at 12-mo. NEW: an ongoing Phase 2 rituximab-pvvr +/- SEQUENTIAL abatacept combo trial (rituximab wk1-4, abatacept from wk16 x20mo) aims to enhance durability - NO results yet. No upgrade; effect remains modest/transient.

rituximab -> nephropathy (DIABETIC).key_finding: No clinical evidence supports rituximab for diabetic nephropathy. The path is a co-occurrence artifact. Rituximab IS validated for membranous nephropathy (PMID 35074299 meta-analysis), but that is a distinct, autoimmune-mediated glomerular disease — NOT diabetic kidney disease.
rituximab -> nephropathy (DIABETIC).reaffirm_note: 2026-07-17: CONTRADICTED reaffirmed. Fresh search returns rituximab RCT evidence only for IgA nephropathy (negative: no proteinuria/eGFR benefit, PMID 27821627) and membranous nephropathy (positive, distinct autoimmune GN); NO diabetic-nephropathy RCT. Path remains a co-occurrence artifact.

Kidney disease progression or CV death 13.1% vs 16.9% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82, p<0.001) in CKD with or without diabetes (n=6,609).

glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.notes: LEADER (liraglutide, PMID 27295427, NEJM 2016): MACE HR 0.87 (0.78-0.97). SUSTAIN-6 (s.c. semaglutide, PMID 27633186, NEJM 2016): MACE HR 0.74 (0.58-0.95). PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide, PMID 31185157, NEJM 2019): MACE HR 0.79 (0.57-1.11), met noninferiority. REWIND (dulaglutide): MACE reduction in primary prevention. 2024 meta-analysis (PMID 38953365) MACE reduction confirmed across patients with and without diabetes. Class effect supported.
glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.caveats: REWIND population had only 31.5% with CVD vs ~70% in others; heterogeneity in dosing and follow-up duration; trial-level analyses not at individual patient level except IPD subset.
glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.revisit_2026-07-26: Re-validated (stalest path, prior 2026-05-08). STRENGTHENED. SOUL trial (PMID 40162642, NEJM 2025-03-29): oral semaglutide in T2D with ASCVD/CKD, MACE HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.77-0.96), P=0.0028 over median 47.5 mo -- upgrades oral-semaglutide evidence from PIONEER 6 noninferiority to demonstrated superiority; nonfatal MI driver (-26%). Supported by 2025 JACC SR/MA of 99,599 patients across 21 trials (10.1016/j.jacc.2025.08.027) confirming consistent class-level MACE benefit incl. non-diabetic obesity (~20% MACE reduction). Rating unchanged: VALIDATED (robust class effect).

pioglitazone -> inflammation.downgrade_reason: Two independent problems found 2026-08-15. (a) CLAIM SCOPE: the stored external claim 'PPARgamma activation reduces hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-alpha independently of glucose lowering' is only partly supported. The largest T2DM-specific pooled analysis (PMID 25897968, 27 RCTs) finds hsCRP and MCP-1 significantly reduced, but IL-6 NOT significant; MMP-9, sCD40L, PAI-1 and ICAM-1 also null. For pioglitazone specifically the authors state it 'reduced serum hsCRP and MCP-1 but had no marked effects on MMP-9, IL-6 and ICAM-1'. PAI-1/vWF/fibrinogen reductions were ROSIGLITAZONE-specific, not pioglitazone. The MA's own conclusion is 'limited evidence'. TNF-alpha was not a pooled endpoint at all - that claim traced to no source. (b) CORPUS SUPPORT IS AN ARTIFACT: the single corpus data point (PMID 35466661) is a hydroxychloroquine SR/MA in which pioglitazone appears only as a comparator-arm dose label ('400 mg OD'). No pioglitazone anti-inflammatory result exists in that paper.

belatacept -> islet_transplant.external_evidence: STRENGTHENED on 2026-08-25 by PMID 42608595 (Rogers NM et al., Diabetologia 2026, Australian Islet Consortium; DOI 10.1007/s00125-026-06813-3; ACTRN12619000268145). This is the first MULTI-CENTRE human test of belatacept+sirolimus in islet transplantation. 9 recipients on bela/siro vs 24 contemporaneous on tac/MMF. Primary composite (freedom from hypoglycaemia, positive C-peptide, HbA1c <53 mmol/mol at 12 months) reached by 8/9 (89%) vs 12 (52%). Renal function was preserved only in the bela/siro arm, which is the specific advantage the calcineurin-sparing rationale predicts. CD4+FOXP3+ Treg proportions were higher on bela/siro. Consistent with the prior single-centre human series (37359825, Posselt 2023, 70% insulin-independent at 10 y across a belatacept/efalizumab cohort) and with non-human-primate work (23347226; 23279640, belatacept+sirolimus prolongs islet allograft survival).
belatacept -> islet_transplant.evidence_quality_change: single-centre, n=5 belatacept  ->  multi-centre, n=9 with a contemporaneous comparator arm. A real improvement in external validity.
belatacept -> islet_transplant.why_not_upgraded_further: The design is NON-RANDOMISED, open-label, phase 2, n=9, 12 months, with a CONTEMPORANEOUS rather than randomised control. Allocation was not concealed and the arms are not guaranteed exchangeable, so the 89% vs 52% contrast cannot be read as a causal treatment effect. 89% is 8 of 9 patients -- one additional failure would make it 78%. The authors write that the results support 'routine use'; this repo does NOT adopt that conclusion, because n=9 non-randomised evidence does not establish a standard of care. Rating stays VALIDATED (the path is real and now multi-centre), it does not become a strong-recommendation claim.
belatacept -> islet_transplant.note: Denominator caveat: the abstract says 24 received tac/MMF but reports 12 as 52%, which implies 23 evaluable. Quote 8/9 vs 12/23-or-24 with that caveat, never a bare '89% vs 52%'.
belatacept -> islet_transplant.evidence_design_why: at least one citing paper reports primary data

NLRP3_inflammasome -> T2D.external_evidence: Strong mechanistic support: islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) oligomers activate the NLRP3 inflammasome -> mature IL-1beta in T2D (Nat Immunol 2010, PMID 20835230); islet macrophage NLRP3-ASC activation mediates beta-cell loss (PMID 23955712). Anti-IL-1beta proof-of-concept studies favorably modulate glycemia.
NLRP3_inflammasome -> T2D.note: One contradicting report (db/db mice: evidence against NLRP3-driven islet inflammation) tempers the islet-specific claim, but obesity/insulin-resistance link is well replicated. Mechanistic, not interventional outcome data.

rapamycin -> islet_transplant.external_evidence: Re-examined 2026-08-25 against PMID 42608595. The new multi-centre study DOES use sirolimus -- but only inside a belatacept+sirolimus combination, compared against tacrolimus+MMF. Sirolimus is therefore CONFOUNDED with belatacept and cannot be credited with the observed benefit.
rapamycin -> islet_transplant.why_not_upgraded: This is the honest reading and it is the opposite of the convenient one. 42608595 was queued as evidence that would strengthen BOTH islet paths. It strengthens belatacept -> islet_transplant, because belatacept is the variable that differs between the arms. It does NOT strengthen rapamycin -> islet_transplant, because no arm isolates sirolimus: there is no belatacept-alone arm and no sirolimus-alone arm. Attributing the 89% to sirolimus would be crediting a co-intervention. The path stays PARTIALLY_VALIDATED on the pre-existing basis (Edmonton-protocol cornerstone agent; Berney 2009 'friend or foe?' review, PMID 18713146), which remains protocol-level rather than comparative evidence.

canagliflozin -> inflammation.evidence: CANTATA-SU: canagliflozin 300mg x52wk lowered IL-6 ~22% and CRP ~4.4% vs glimepiride in T2D. SGLT2i meta-analysis (18 studies, n=5311) shows significant IL-6 reduction. Mechanistic: canagliflozin inhibits IL-6 release in LPS-stimulated endothelial/immune cells via hexokinase II / autophagy.

Treg_expansion -> T1D.mechanism: Low-dose IL-2 selectively engages high-affinity trimeric IL-2R on CD4+ Tregs, expanding thymic Tregs and CD56bright NK, reducing IL-21+ CD4 T cells, shifting Treg/Teff balance toward regulation; durable anti-inflammatory signature ~1mo post-treatment.

external_evidence.Hartemann/NCT02411253: ld-rhIL-2 safe, expands Tregs; NOT powered for efficacy.
external_evidence.PMC9705541 Nat Commun 2022: ld-IL2 reduces IL-21+ T cells, anti-inflammatory signature in T1D.

Treg_expansion -> T1D.note: 2026-06-26 web re-validation: REAFFIRMED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. No new efficacy-powered RCT since 2026-06-16. T-Rex phase 2 (Sci Transl Med 2024, scitranslmed.adn2404 / PMID 38718135): single-dose expanded polyclonal Tregs SAFE but did NOT preserve C-peptide in new-onset pediatric T1D. ld-IL-2 paradoxical dissociation persists (Treg expansion + HbA1c signal without consistent C-peptide preservation; vs immunotherapy preserving C-peptide without HbA1c benefit). Target engagement (Treg expansion, safety) robust in humans; durable clinical beta-cell preservation from Treg expansion alone remains unproven. Capped at PARTIALLY until an efficacy-powered RCT reads out.

metformin -> nephropathy.evidence: Cohort/meta evidence: metformin associated with lower creatinine doubling (HR ~0.71), eGFR<=15 (HR ~0.61) and ESKD (HR ~0.55); slower eGFR decline across subgroups. Mechanism via AMPK, reduced renal inflammation/oxidative stress. Note: observational, not RCT-grade for renal endpoints; SGLT2i/GLP-1 are guideline add-ons for DKD.

eClinicalMedicine 2024 target-trial emulation (Hong Kong, PIIS2589-5370(24)00147-0) - metformin DISCONTINUATION in advanced CKD assoc. higher ESKD risk (HR 1.52)

Web sweep 2026-08-05 added: (a) MET-EMPA-CKD 2025 RCT (metformin vs empagliflozin on CKD progression) - first head-to-head RCT touching this axis, but active-comparator design vs an established renoprotective agent, NOT metformin-vs-placebo for hard renal endpoints, so does NOT upgrade to RCT-grade renoprotection proof; (b) eClinicalMedicine 2024 territory-wide target-trial emulation - discontinuing metformin in advanced CKD assoc. oxidative_stress -> T2D.evidence: Banik 2021 SR/MA (Health Sci Rep, PMID 34622023): 22 case-control studies, 2853 subjects; MDA & nitric oxide elevated, glutathione/total antioxidant status reduced in T2D vs controls. Pathogenic association well-supported. CAVEAT: antioxidant-supplementation RCTs have failed to show glycemic/prevention benefit, so association is robust but therapeutic causality unproven. | 2026-06-30 reaffirmed with fresh therapeutic-side evidence: resveratrol meta-analysis (Front Endocrinol 2024, DOI 10.3389/fendo.2024.1463027, PMC11771208; 6 RCTs, n=533) shows resveratrol significantly lowered CRP, lipid peroxides and 8-isoprostanes and raised GPx/catalase in T2D, BUT malondialdehyde, SOD, total antioxidant capacity, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were NOT significantly changed. NET: pathogenic oxidative-stress association remains robust; antioxidant-therapy signal is partial/marker-selective and therapeutic causality still unproven. Rating unchanged: VALIDATED (association), therapy=PARTIAL. | 2026-07-25 therapy-arm re-validation: THREE new 2025-26 RCT meta-analyses located. (1) Brandimonte-Hernandez/Gil, Nutrition Reviews 2026, DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuaf292 (advance access; PMID pending) - 109 human RCTs of food bioactive compounds: alpha-lipoic acid and vitamin D produced SIGNIFICANT HbA1c reductions; zinc/selenium/chromium improved glycemic control + raised total antioxidant capacity/enzyme activity. (2) Vitamin C/E subgroup MA, Nutrition Reviews 2026, DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuaf133 (PMC12793614): high-antioxidant-capacity C/E inversely associated with insulin resistance but agent/dose/duration dependent. (3) Astaxanthin MA 2026, DOI 10.1177/11786388261432862, 9 RCTs n=403 prediabetes/T2D: glycemic+lipid signal. NET: pathogenic association remains ROBUST (VALIDATED). Therapy-side signal is STRENGTHENED but remains AGENT-SPECIFIC (ALA, vit-D, Zn/Se/Cr show HbA1c benefit) and heterogeneous; classic antioxidant vitamins (C/E alone) stay weak. Therapy rating = PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (upgraded from marker-selective PARTIAL: now at least two agents show a hard glycemic endpoint, HbA1c). Therapeutic causality for 'antioxidants broadly' still unproven.

tacrolimus -> inflammation.evidence: REAFFIRMED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (re-checked 2026-06-23). Bidirectional/context-dependent. Anti-inflammatory in T cells: tacrolimus inhibits NF-kB activation in peripheral human T cells (PLOS One, PMID 23573283), suppressing IL-2/TNFa/IL-6. Pro-inflammatory in vasculature: CNIs (tacrolimus, cyclosporine A) induce vascular inflammation & endothelial activation via TLR4 signaling -> increased ROS and NF-kB-regulated proinflammatory factors in endothelial/VSMCs; effect abolished in TLR4-/- aortas (Sci Rep srep27915, PMID 27295076 - corrected from prior 27291296). Net effect on inflammation NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory.
tacrolimus -> inflammation.note: No promotion - inherently context-dependent. PMID corrected: vascular-inflammation paper is 27295076 (was 27291296 in earlier note).
tacrolimus -> inflammation.revisit_2026_07_03: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (context-dependent). Fresh 2025 source added: Pharmacological Reports 2025 review "Tacrolimus and diabetic rodent models" (PMID 39836342) - 48 studies; tacrolimus impairs islet beta-cell function via CaN/NFAT, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-beta/Smad and catalogs anti-inflammatory/antioxidant agents used to counter tacrolimus-induced diabetes, reinforcing pro-inflammatory/diabetogenic side. Vascular TLR4 pro-inflammatory paper (PMID 27295076) reaffirmed, no 2025-26 contradiction. Net effect NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory -> no promotion.
tacrolimus -> inflammation.revisit_2026_08_06: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (context-dependent, no promotion). Anti-inflammatory arm strengthened: 2025 narrative review 'Clinical applications of tacrolimus in ocular diseases' (PMID 41264132, Int Ophthalmol 2025) reiterates FKBP-12/calcineurin/NFAT inhibition suppressing IL-2 and pro-inflammatory cytokines and modulating Th17/Treg balance. Pro-inflammatory arm gained an independent second source: PMID 23958496 (CNIs recruit JAK2/JNK, TLR signaling and UPR to activate NF-kB-mediated inflammation in kidney tubular cells), complementing the vascular TLR4 finding (PMID 27295076). No 2025-26 contradiction of the bidirectional picture. Net effect NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory -> remains PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

GAD65 -> T1D.notes: DECISIVE NEGATIVE. The largest, HLA-enriched, confirmatory phase 3 of the hub-tracked antigen-specific tolerance strategy failed. Sponsor-offered contributing hypotheses (intralymphatic administration burden at low-volume sites; longer diagnosis-to-treatment interval; lower drug-product potency than DIAGNODE-2) are EXPLICITLY hypothesis-generating per the sponsor and must NOT be reported as established explanations. Subgroup numerical trends were underpowered and exploratory. SCOPE LIMIT: this contradicts MONOTHERAPY in recent-onset T1D. It does NOT directly test (a) LADA, where no pivotal data exist, (b) combination regimens (GAD-alum + vitamin D + etanercept), or (c) Stage 1/2 prevention. Downstream: GAD65-targeted CAR-Treg work is a different modality and is unaffected. NO peer-reviewed publication of DIAGNODE-3 exists yet - watch item.

colchicine -> inflammation.notes: CONFIDENCE CUT HIGH -> MEDIUM on 2026-08-20, and the source list rebuilt. The former lead source "Exploration Pub 2025 - New perspectives on NLRP3 inflammasome-colchicine and metabolic syndrome" is NOT PubMed-indexed and could not be resolved to a PMID by title, journal or author search; it is DROPPED. A citation nobody can look up cannot carry a HIGH rating. What replaces it is stronger in one dimension and weaker in another. Stronger: PMID 41889274 is a diabetes-specific meta-analysis of 5 RCTs on a HARD endpoint (MACE), which the path previously lacked entirely. Weaker: the path as written is colchicine -> INFLAMMATION, and 41889274 measures cardiovascular events, not inflammatory markers. The direct marker-level evidence IN A DIABETES POPULATION is still thin. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: PMID 36643381 (Biomed Hub 2022, low-dose colchicine on hs-CRP in CAD+T2DM) surfaced in the search and looks like exactly the missing evidence, but it is a PROTOCOL paper - "patients WILL BE randomly assigned", no results reported. Recorded here so a future run does not re-find it and mistake it for a results publication. alpha_lipoic_acid -> diabetic_neuropathy.notes: SPLIT BY ROUTE - this is the whole finding. IV 600 mg/day x 3 weeks produces a significant and clinically relevant reduction in neuropathic pain. ORAL >600 mg/day for 3-5 weeks shows statistically significant change whose CLINICAL relevance is unclear. Rated PARTIALLY_VALIDATED, not VALIDATED, because (a) the pivotal MAs are 2012-vintage, (b) the practical route for chronic outpatient care is oral - the weaker arm, (c) endpoints are symptom scores and nerve-conduction velocity, i.e. surrogate/subjective, with no hard outcome such as ulceration or amputation. Safety profile favourable (mainly stomach upset).

GLP1_RA -> neuroprotection.notes: DOWNGRADED 2026-08-20: VALIDATED/HIGH -> PARTIALLY_VALIDATED/LOW. This path was the single worst case found by the bare-string audit - rated HIGH confidence on zero resolvable PMIDs, and when the strings were resolved the flagship citation turned out to be a NEGATIVE TRIAL. ELAD (PMID 41326666) missed its primary endpoint (P = 0.14) and was null on both functional/global secondaries (ADCS-ADL P = 0.65, CDR-SoB P = 0.81). The one positive, ADAS-Exec, rests on an unadjusted P = 0.01 across a multi-endpoint battery. The widely circulated "18% slower cognitive decline / ~50% less brain atrophy" figures are EXPLORATORY outputs reported in press coverage, not in the trials stated endpoint hierarchy - they must not be cited as trial results. The stored note previously read "2025 phase 2b liraglutide AD trial + large propensity-matched cohorts show 40-70% lower dementia incidence", which fuses a negative RCT and positive observational cohorts into one apparent body of converging evidence. The 40-70% figure comes ONLY from the cohorts. Corrected. RELEVANCE CAVEAT, separate from the statistics: ELAD enrolled participants with NO DIABETES. Its bearing on a diabetes corpus is indirect at best. What remains: one negative RCT, two observational datasets subject to confounding by indication, and one narrative review. That supports "biologically plausible, clinically unproven" - which is PARTIALLY_VALIDATED / LOW, not VALIDATED / HIGH. DECIDING EVIDENCE PENDING: EVOKE / EVOKE+ (semaglutide, phase 3, AD). Those readouts are what would move this path, not another cohort study.

Effect present in patients with and without T2D. dapagliflozin -> T2D.evidence_summary: Landmark indication for dapagliflozin in T2D — VALIDATED. DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NEJM 2019, PMID 30415602; n=17,160 T2D patients, median 4.2 y follow-up): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo MET non-inferiority for MACE (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.84-1.03; p=0.17 for superiority) and was SUPERIOR for the co-primary composite of CV death/HF hospitalization (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73-0.95; p=0.005), driven primarily by HF-hospitalization reduction (HR 0.73). Cardiorenal secondary composite (Mosenzon Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2019, PMID 31196815): HR 0.76 (0.67-0.87); renal-specific composite excluding CV death HR 0.53 (0.43-0.66). Effect consistent in patients with and without established CVD; benefit present in preserved-EF and reduced-EF subgroups. Multi-trial SGLT2i SR/MA (Zelniker Lancet 2019; updated 2024-2025 meta-analyses) places DECLARE alongside EMPA-REG, CANVAS, CREDENCE, EMPEROR, DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD as collectively defining SGLT2i benefit in T2D for cardio-renal outcomes. ADA Standards of Care 2025 list dapagliflozin as guideline-recommended in T2D with established/at-risk CVD, HF, or CKD. | 2026-07-18 reaffirmation: no contradicting evidence; SGLT2i cardiorenal benefit remains ADA-guideline-standard. Linked kidney-outcome durability further supported by NDT 2024 time-to-event analysis (PMID 38730538). Rating unchanged VALIDATED (STRONG).
caveats: DAPA-HF and DAPA-CKD established benefit in patients without diabetes too — the dapagliflozin->T2D label has expanded into broader cardiorenal indications.

DECLARE was not powered for kidney hard endpoints (kidney-specific composite a secondary analysis); DAPA-CKD provides the dedicated kidney-outcome RCT (already validated separately as dapagliflozin_nephropathy).

audit_notes.title: PubMed publication type - the design grader's only input - is silently incomplete, in both directions
audit_notes.detail: audit_path_evidence_design.py grades every path on PubMed pubtype, justified as "the one field a builder cannot accidentally invent". True, but PubMed can OMIT it, and the grader reads absence as unknown design. Reading the 16 PRIMARY_OTHER papers found the omission running BOTH ways in one batch. PMID 36643381 (Biomed Hub 2022) has "Protocol for a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2, Dose-Finding Study" in its title and pubtype [Journal Article] only: it reports no results and supplies 7 live extractions. PMID 36826844 (JAMA 2023) has "A Randomized Clinical Trial" in its title and pubtype [Journal Article, Research Support Non-U.S. Govt]: it is CLVer, n=88, it MEASURED 52-week C-peptide, and it supplies 0 extractions. Net effect on this corpus: 39613428 (Ver-A-T1D protocol, no results) is the single largest contributor at 15 of 232 live extractions, 36643381 adds 7, and the randomised trial that actually measured the outcome contributes none. Coverage measured across all 359 cached papers: 134 (37%) carry no design-bearing pubtype at all, rising from ~31% pre-2018 to 46% for 2025 and 66% for 2026 papers. PubMed assigns design tags on a lag, so the grader is blindest on exactly the papers the daily sweeps keep adding. New gate: audit_pubtype_title_disagreement.py, wired before pathdesign. It compares the VERIFIED title against the pubtype field and reports, never applies.

audit_notes.title: A citation can be right about its paper and wrong about what the paper says: 47 sites, one PMID
audit_notes.detail: build_drug_repurposing_screen.py attributed the monthly cost of all 34 screened drugs, the cost chart, the cost bars, the stat card, the availability-score thresholds, the five combination-cost cells and the methodology paragraph to "Hernandez 2018 (PMID:29710129) generic drug pricing" - 47 sites. Every identifier is CORRECT: the PMID resolves, the first author is Hernandez, the year is 2018, the title agrees with PubMed. It is Hernandez I, Prasad V, Gellad WF, "Total Costs of Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Immunotherapy", JAMA Oncol 2018;4(7):994-996 - a research letter on CAR-T therapy costs, holding no generic drug price. build_cart_access.py cites the same PMID correctly in a CAR-T context; the screen appears to have borrowed the identifier. The methodology paragraph was worst: it DESCRIBED the paper as a "systematic review of global generic drug pricing", which tells a reader what they would have found had they checked. Every existing gate is silent by construction - PMID validation, title agreement, coordinate checking and the retraction gate all test whether a citation IDENTIFIES the right paper, and it does. audit_prose_citation_titles.py did see it, at line 41, and filed it under journal_not_recognised (a gate-artifact bucket) because the citation string names no journal to compare. EIGHTH defect class: the citation is correct and the claim is not. Repair marked all 47 sites UNSOURCED; no substitute source was invented and no cost VALUE was changed. It took three passes - two reported success while the same claim survived in differently-worded captions ("WHO generic drug databases" vs "WHO pricing databases"). A wrong source spreads by paraphrase; only grep for the bare identifier cleared it.

audit_notes.title: The 2026-08-28 P1 item named the wrong page; the count-vs-quality inversion is published as a PROBABILITY
audit_notes.detail: The queue item said "the published Research Paths dashboard still orders by count alone". Checked and FALSE: that page sorted on (status, confidence, name) and, every path there being VALIDATED/HIGH, it resolved to ALPHABETICAL. Count decided nothing on it. The real count-derived ranking is on the STATISTICAL ANALYSIS page, where statistical_analysis.py::bayesian_path_scoring sets the prior purely from data_point_count and PMID count - neither the prior nor the likelihood reads study design. Measured: 48 of 77 comparable ordered pairs (62.3%) are DISCORDANT, and 16 of those rank a NO_RESULTS path above a path resting on primary data. Published: verapamil->T1D 40.0% and verapamil->beta_cell 40.0% (both protocol-only) above dapagliflozin->nephropathy 26.4%, oxidative_stress->cardiovascular 26.4% and rapamycin->inflammation 26.4% (all PRIMARY). A sorted list invites a reader to infer a ranking; a posterior states one. Actions: tier badges and design-first ordering wired into build_research_paths.py; full discordance disclosure printed ABOVE the Bayesian ranking; NO_RESULTS paths capped at strength INSUFFICIENT with the uncapped value shown beside it. The prior was NOT refit - what a prior encodes is a modelling decision and is carried to the queue as a human call. Also corrected on the page: the "High Confidence Validated Paths" heading claimed "the strongest evidence base from systematic reviews and/or landmark RCTs" while listing two protocol-only paths.

audit_notes.title: The site advertised 41 links it could not serve, and the publish step was what broke 34 of them
audit_notes.detail: audit_published_links.py (new today) resolved every relative href/src in docs/**.html against the filesystem: 1359 resolved, 41 did not. THE BULK IS ONE DEFECT. postprocess_dashboards.py inserts a "<- Hub" back-link as href="../docs/index.html", which is correct at Dashboards/X.html and wrong at docs/Dashboards/X.html, where it resolves to docs/docs/index.html. All 34 published dashboards carried it. THE REASON IT SURVIVED SINCE 2026-08-16 IS THE VERIFICATION ITSELF: sync_docs_dashboards.py verified byte equality between source and published copy, and byte equality is exactly what guarantees this defect - a depth-relative link MUST differ between depths for both to work. A copy step that verifies sameness cannot detect a defect whose fix is difference. Also found: three hand-written nav links (build_drug_repurposing_screen "Home", build_lada_diagnostic_model "<- Back to Index", build_trial_equity_mapper "<- Dashboard Home") pointing at a docs/Dashboards/index.html that has never existed, one build_corpus_analysis href="/" pointing at the Pages DOMAIN root rather than this project, and the two hub report cards below. FIXED: the four builders now emit the repo-root form; sync_docs_dashboards.py declares a PUBLISH_REWRITES table, applies it on copy and verifies against the transformed text; audit_published_links.py is wired as the last pipeline stage. 41 -> 0.

THE UNDERLYING STALENESS IS NOT FIXED and is queued: a "rolling 30-day snapshot" that is 49 days old is a live claim the pipeline is not refreshing.

audit_notes.title: Two gaps had never been audited on their own question; both survive it
audit_notes.detail: Gaps #4 (Drug Repurposing for Islet Transplant) and #5 (Treg in Diabetic Neuropathy) carry 0% topic overlap across all 5 prior audits each - their trails are each other's and a third topic's. Their SILVER tiers had never rested on evidence about their own questions. Both audited on-topic today with bounded PubMed queries and both hold. Notably BOTH on-topic audits surfaced a near-miss that a looser reading would have logged as gap closure: PMID 39911401 is a genuine repurposing screen validated in mouse SKIN grafts, not islets, and PMID 42486100 is a cost-motivated CAR-NK Phase I in SLE, not diabetes. The gap set's exposure is not that audits find nothing - it is that an audit reading only search-result summaries would have closed two gaps today on papers about the wrong tissue and the wrong disease.

PUBLISH REACHABILITY MEASURED, NOT JUST NOTED. git fetch SUCCEEDS in the sandbox (public remote, read needs no credential) - only push lacks credentials. That makes the divergence quantifiable for the first time: 101 commits unpushed, origin/main tip f7e976f 2026-04-20 (138d), and under the publish root 38 of 39 files are wrong for a reader - 4 return 404 (Islet_Drug_Repurposing.html, Prediction_Ledger.html, Reports/literature_gap_report.md, Reports/pubmed_recent_summary.md) and 34 are stale copies. Exactly 1 of 39 files is what this pipeline believes it published.

ABSENCE CLAIMS ARE THE ONE CLAIM CLASS NO CITATION GATE CAN SEE, because they are produced by finding nothing and so have no citation to check. 17 unscoped absence claims were live across docs/ and Dashboards/. Re-running each all-time falsified two: 'Treg-based therapy has never been tested for diabetic neuropathy' (PMID 42698953, published 2 days before the check, plus PMID 39084449) and 'generic drugs have never been systematically evaluated for repurposing' (PMID 37399599). Three survived all-time and are now scope-stamped (GKA x LADA 0 records; personalized nutrition x beta cell preservation 0; CAR-T equity x diabetes immunotherapy 4 records, none on point). One - 'computational drug screening has not been applied to islet transplant' - is TRUE beside a pair_count of 0 that is FALSE (7 all-time records, none a screen): the right conclusion for an evidence-free reason, which nothing downstream could distinguish from a verified claim.

A GATE THAT DESTROYS EVIDENCE TO ENFORCE CONSISTENCY IS WORSE THAN THE INCONSISTENCY. audit_verdict_key_agreement.py's first run reported 3 self-contradicting records and its --fix would have corrupted one: paths['atorvastatin -> T2D'] holds status CONTRADICTED beside rating VALIDATED_AS_RISK_FACTOR, which are one answer each to two different propositions (does it treat T2D / does it cause T2D), the latter backed by Sattar 2010 PMID 19794004, IPD meta of 13 trials and 91,140 patients, +9% incident T2D. Conservative resolution would have overwritten a correct finding. Gate now classifies off-vocabulary verdicts as VERDICT_SCOPE_MISMATCH and refuses to auto-resolve them.

audit_notes.severity: HIGH - reader-facing, on a published dashboard, four independently checkable errors on one citation
audit_notes.found: The Gap #11 evidence catalog described PMID 19104422 as: "Comprehensive data on 1,477 transplant recipients ... Published biennially in American Journal of Transplantation. Barton et al. An update on results of the International Islet Transplant Registry." Checked against live PubMed on 2026-09-08, PMID 19104422 is Alejandro R, Barton FB, Hering BJ, Wease S, "2008 Update from the Collaborative Islet Transplant Registry", Transplantation 2008 Dec 27;86(12):1783-8, reporting 325 recipients / 649 infusions / 712 donors. Wrong first author, wrong title, wrong journal, wrong denominator, wrong registry (the International Islet Transplant Registry was a separate registry, not CITR). The 1,477 figure belongs to the CITR 12th Allograft Report (2025), a registry PDF at citregistry.org covering 1999-2023 across 40 centres - no PMID, not peer-reviewed. SECOND ERROR, same page: the "85% White recipients" bar carried an inline PMID:19104422 link. That abstract reports no racial or ethnic breakdown at all. The comparator figures (62% / 5% / 18% / 5% / 20%) carried no citation whatsoever. THIRD ERROR, same page: the "What This Cannot Tell You" block asserted "GOLD tier (3+ independent sources)" while the hub card for the same dashboard said SILVER - a third writer of the tier, disagreeing with the other two.
audit_notes.fixed: Split the evidence-catalog entry in two: a CITR Allograft Reports entry carrying the 1,477 figure, explicitly labelled registry-grade and not peer-reviewed, and a correct entry for PMID 19104422 with its real authors, journal, year and n=325, carrying a visible correction notice. Removed the PMID:19104422 attribution from the 85% bar and replaced the block's source line with a visible UNSOURCED warning naming every uncited figure and stating what a citable replacement would require. Changed the in-page tier from GOLD to SILVER and added the measured 0-record search result.
audit_notes.not_fixed: No replacement citation was invented for 85% / 62% / 5% / 18% / 5% / 20%. The numbers are left on the page marked UNSOURCED rather than deleted, because deleting them would hide that the dashboard was making the claim. Sourcing them requires reading a CITR Allograft Report recipient-characteristics table directly and transcribing it with its denominator and reporting year. Queued.

audit_notes.mechanism: corpus_membership.excluded_pmids() assigns the code FLAGGED_UNCLASSIFIED to any PMID that is FLAGGED in agent_state with no membership_class recorded, and treats it as adjudicated NOT A CORPUS PAPER. reconcile_paper_index.py then evicts it from index.json. So "flagged for review" and "adjudicated off-topic" are the same act, though they are opposite judgements: one says look closer, the other says this does not belong.

audit_notes.finding: THE GIT BLOCK WAS NEVER A MOUNT LIMITATION ON WRITING. IT WAS TWO STALE LOCK FILES, AND RENAMING THEM MAKES ORDINARY git commit WORK.
audit_notes.detail: The 2026-09-16 workaround (GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the mount) treats the symptom. What actually blocked today was .git/HEAD.lock (left 2026-09-18) and .git/index.lock (left 2026-09-17). unlink is forbidden on this OneDrive mount but RENAME is not, so `mv .git/HEAD.lock .git/HEAD.lock.stale` and the same for index.lock cleared both, after which a plain `git add -A` + `git commit` with the DEFAULT index succeeded: commit 9b6b6a3, 127 files, porcelain 0. GIT_INDEX_FILE was not needed and in fact masked the real blocker - with it set, `git add` succeeded and `git commit` still failed, because the lock git could not take was HEAD.lock, not the index.
audit_notes.evidence_of_how_long: .git now holds 203 renamed lock files dating back to 2026-04-10 - HEAD.lock.gone2, index.lock.delete-me, index.lock.evicted4, and so on. Every run since April has fought this and left debris. The recurring "SANDBOX FAILURE" queue items at priority 0 describe this.
audit_notes.applied: Both locks renamed at the start and the fresh ones left by today's commit renamed again at the end, so tomorrow starts clean.

doctrine_notes.pmid_threshold_2026-05-04: The doctrine heuristic "PMIDs above 42000000 = fabricated" needs revision. As of 2026-05-04, real PMIDs are in the 42M range (verified via NCBI E-utilities esummary endpoint). The 42M threshold was likely set when PubMed counts were lower. Going forward, verify suspected fabrications via E-utilities lookup, not by PMID number alone.
doctrine_notes.pmid_range_2026: As of 2026-05-05, NCBI is assigning PMIDs in the 42,000,000+ range for current 2026 publications. The legacy SKILL.md credibility-sweep heuristic flagging PMIDs > 42,000,000 is stale and produces false positives for legitimately recent papers. PMIDs must still be verified via NCBI esummary, but the numeric ceiling alone is not a fabrication signal. Updated 2026-05-05.
doctrine_notes.credibility_sweep_2026-05-07: DEPRECATED ceiling-only PMID > 42,000,000 fabrication test in favor of: (1) round-trip via NCBI esummary for any new PMID, (2) cross-reference against agent_state.json papers map (single source of truth), (3) flag only if year > current year + 1.
