Validation statuses, external_pmids, validation_notes merged, preferring stronger status. SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD retained as 3-way path.
doctrine_notes.credibility_2026_07_02: A DOI recorded in a prior run (Ver-A-T1D Diabetologia) failed independent web re-confirmation. Practice: flag single-source DOIs as UNVERIFIED until directly hit, rather than propagating.
doctrine_notes.pmid_range_reconfirm_2026_07_10: Reconfirmation of pmid_threshold_2026-05-04 / pmid_range_2026: the '>42,000,000 PMID = fabricated' heuristic remains STALE. On 2026-07-10 the live NCBI esummary API returned real records for 42220535 (Front Immunol 2026), 42203900 (Bone Marrow Transplant 2026, EBMT activity report), and 42218679 (Magyar Onkologia 2026). These IDs exist ONLY in non-published scratch file Analysis/Results/_audit_2026-06-02_gap_2_3_6.json and are referenced by no live script/dashboard/doc; the numeric ceiling is not hardcoded in any .py. Operative fabrication gate stays live-API verification (verify_pmids.py: 262/262 today). Do NOT delete these IDs.
doctrine_notes.pmid_cutoff_heuristic: As of 2026-07-25 the SKILL Step-4 rule 'PMIDs >42000000 = fabricated' is STALE and produces FALSE POSITIVES. PubMed sequential IDs legitimately reach the 42.0-42.2M range by mid-2026. State currently holds 13 REAL eutils-verified papers with PMIDs in 42021540-42160884 (e.g. 42113684 = Diabetes/ADA DOI 10.2337/db25-0933; 42160884 = J Autoimmun). Correct fabrication test is NOT a fixed numeric cutoff but: (a) does the PMID resolve via NCBI eutils, and (b) does its title/journal/year match the state record. Apply that test; do not auto-flag on the 42M threshold alone. Re-baseline the numeric tripwire to ~>43000000 for the next few months and re-check quarterly.
doctrine_notes.pmid_threshold_reconfirm_2026-08-08: 2026-08-08: Re-confirmed the >=42M PMID heuristic is STALE. This run: 2,426 distinct >=42M PMIDs appear ONLY in raw pubmed_recent_snapshot_*.json API dumps + derived monitor reports (all real April-2026 records); ZERO >=42M PMIDs cited in any build/dashboard .py (max script-cited=41921761). Step-4 sweep (scope=.py scripts) CLEAN.
doctrine_notes.extraction_artifact_comparator_arms_2026: SYSTEMATIC EXTRACTION FLAW (found 2026-08-15). Drug names appearing in the trial-characteristics tables of systematic reviews / meta-analyses - i.e. as COMPARATOR or BACKGROUND therapy - are extracted as if they were the SUBJECT of a mechanistic claim, creating false 'drug -> outcome' paths. Single source PMID 35466661 (HCQ SR/MA) alone generated 5 such paths: atorvastatin->T2D, metformin->inflammation, pioglitazone->inflammation, pioglitazone->T2D, hydroxychloroquine->inflammation. The 2026-05-14 filter in build_research_paths.py caught only 3 because it required data_point_count==1; paths with repeated dose fragments (including an exact DUPLICATE fragment inflating dpc from 1 to 3) escaped. FIXED 2026-08-15: is_dose_fragment_artifact() now fires whenever EVERY key_claim is a non-mechanistic dose fragment, at any dpc. LESSON: data_point_count is NOT a proxy for evidential weight when the points can be duplicates from one table. Audit any path whose corpus_pmids is a single SR/MA.
doctrine_notes.pmid_verification_sweep_2026-08-15: Full-corpus verification: all 287 PMIDs round-tripped through NCBI esummary in one bulk pass. 287/287 resolved; 0 unresolvable; 0 real title drift (1 abbreviation, PMID 35098372). Closed 11 papers that had been carried with pmid_verified=false since 2026-05-02/03. The 13 corpus PMIDs above the legacy 42M 'fabrication' tripwire are all REAL 2026 records - reconfirming for the 5th time that the numeric cutoff is stale. Bulk esummary (100 IDs/request) is far cheaper than per-paper web search; make it the default vetting method.

2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.title: A working detector whose output nobody read
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.finding: validate_citations.py had been correctly scoring miscited PMIDs as MISMATCH and writing them to citation_validation.json - for months. Nothing consumed that field. The daily credibility sweep only grepped for PMIDs >= 42,000,000 and for forbidden phrases, so it reported CLEAN on every run while 7 genuine miscitations sat in the build scripts, two of which resolved to PLANT BIOLOGY papers being cited as the DIAGNODE-2 trial and a GAD-alum meta-analysis.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.root_cause: Detection was decoupled from enforcement. The sweep tested for FABRICATED identifiers (out-of-range PMIDs) but never for MISATTRIBUTED ones - a real PMID pointing at the wrong paper passes every range check.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.secondary_finding: This also explains a long-standing open question: several off-topic oncology/infectious-disease papers sat in the corpus FLAGGED as "unclear relevance to diabetes research". They were ingested BECAUSE they were miscited. The flagged papers were the symptom; the miscitations were the cause.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.fix: Added Analysis/Scripts/check_citation_mismatches.py - a gate that reads citation_validation.json and exits non-zero on any unwhitelisted MISMATCH. Registered in run_quality_improvements.py immediately after validate. Suppression requires a written reason in WHITELIST (currently one entry: a regex example, not a citation).
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.generalisation: Any detector this hub runs must have a consumer that can FAIL. An unread report is not a control.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.ordering_lesson: The claim inventory is cached in pmid_verification.json / paper_library/index.json. Editing a build script is NOT enough - verify_pmids.py -> ingest_papers.py -> build_paper_library.py -> validate_citations.py must be re-run in that order or the validator re-reports already-fixed mismatches.

2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.title: Queue re-validated the validated and ignored the never-validated
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.finding: 14 of 57 research paths had NEVER been validated, while the work queue kept cycling re-validation of paths already rated VALIDATED. The "pick the stalest path" heuristic only ranks paths that already have a validation date, so a path with no date at all is invisible to it forever.
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.fix: Never-validated paths given priority 2 in the queue this run, ahead of re-validation of already-rated paths.
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.note: A prior alias-collision worry was checked and is NOT a real problem: only dorzagliatin->T2D is double-keyed.

2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.title: Green pipeline, frozen public site
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.finding: docs/Dashboards/ - the copy GitHub Pages serves - had not changed since 2026-03-29/2026-04-20. 33 published dashboards stale, 2 missing, ZERO in sync, while run_quality_improvements.py reported "All 42 improvements completed successfully" on every daily run for roughly four months.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.root_cause: rebuild_website.py only ever wrote docs/index.html. No step copied rebuilt dashboards into docs/. The runner measured builder exit codes, not whether the published artifact changed.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.impact: The seven PMID miscitations corrected this run were still live publicly until this was fixed, as was a DIAGNODE-3 description superseded by the trial being closed for futility.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.fix: Added Analysis/Scripts/sync_docs_dashboards.py (copy + byte-equality re-verify, non-zero exit on failure), registered LAST in run_quality_improvements.py - after postprocess_dashboards.py, which rewrites Dashboards/*.html. Supports --check for drift-only reporting. 35/35 now in sync.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.generalisation: Same failure class as the citation MISMATCH gap found the same day: a step reporting success while the artifact a reader actually sees goes untouched. Verify the OUTPUT changed, not that the PRODUCER exited zero.

doctrine_notes.2026-08-17_state_integrity: THREE parallel path stores exist and had drifted: state["paths"] (57), state["validated_paths"] (59), and Analysis/Results/validated_research_paths.json (reports paths_validated=27). 16 paths were in state["paths"] but absent from state["validated_paths"]; 18 the reverse. The work-queue generator reads only ONE store, which is why the 2026-08-16 run emitted six "NEVER-VALIDATED" items for paths that had documented validations (SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD 2026-04-24, teplizumab->autoimmune 2026-05-12, GLP1_RA->T1D 2026-06-21, etc). Stores reconciled this run. The dashboard figure "27 validated" understates the true count and should be regenerated from the reconciled store, not hardcoded.
doctrine_notes.2026-08-17_git_rootcause: GIT BLOCKER ROOT-CAUSED AND PARTLY FIXED - prior diagnosis was WRONG. It was recorded for 3 weeks as "a stale index.lock needing one manual delete". It is not. The OneDrive mount denies unlink() on files inside .git at ANY age (tested at 0s/20s/60s: all BLOCKED), so git cannot complete its write-index-lock-then-rename sequence and leaves a fresh lock behind on EVERY invocation. Deleting the lock on the host would have fixed exactly one run - which is why ~150 renamed lock corpses have accumulated in .git/ since April. WORKAROUND THAT WORKS: set GIT_INDEX_FILE to a path outside the mount (e.g. /tmp/gitidx) - git then writes its index off-mount, and objects/refs (create-new and rename-over, both permitted) succeed. Verified this run: 92 files staged, commit 3a737ed created, ending an 80-commit 3-week backlog. REMAINING BLOCKER IS DIFFERENT AND SMALLER: push fails with "could not read Username for https://github.com" - credentials only, no token in the sandbox. Commit is now automatable; push still needs the user. UPDATE (end of run): `git commit` succeeds only INTERMITTENTLY even with GIT_INDEX_FILE, because commit still touches .git/index.lock. The DETERMINISTIC recipe is plumbing + direct ref write, now codified in Analysis/Scripts/git_commit_safe.py: (1) GIT_INDEX_FILE off-mount, (2) git add -A, (3) git write-tree, (4) git commit-tree, (5) write .git/refs/heads/main by writing a temp file and os.rename() over it - NOT `git update-ref`, which needs HEAD.lock and fails. GOTCHA: write-tree/commit-tree print "unable to unlink tmp_obj_*" warnings onto stdout, so the SHA must be regex-extracted, not read via .strip(). ALL FUTURE RUNS SHOULD CALL git_commit_safe.py INSTEAD OF `git commit`. Confirmed working: commit 9437b70.
doctrine_notes.2026-08-21: A REGEX WITH AN UNBOUNDED WILDCARD IS NOT AN EXTRACTOR, IT IS A RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR. The inflammatory_markers patterns ended in `.*?(\d+\.?\d*)` - no distance bound, no sentence boundary, no unit requirement - so the capture group took the first digit anywhere downstream of the marker name. In immunology prose that digit is almost never a measurement: it is the 3 in NLRP3, the 1 in IL-1, a publication year, a section number, a sample size. 85 of 92 extractions were artifacts, and they were the entire evidence base of the site's top-ranked research path. GENERAL RULE, now applied: a numeric extraction must be bounded by a sentence boundary AND anchored to a unit, a percent tied to a direction verb, or a fold-change token. A number with no unit is not a measurement. Corollary that cost four separate patches today: suppression applied in one place is not suppression - the same hollow path was still live in the validated-path store, the validation summary counter, and the Bayesian ranking after being removed from the path dashboard.
doctrine_notes.2026-08-22: A regex is a claim about language and must be measured like one. The unbounded lazy wildcard `.*?` between a marker token and a capture group has now produced a majority-artifact extractor every single time it has been measured: inflammatory_markers 57% (2026-08-21), then survival_graft 100%, c_peptide 100%, remission 71%, autoantibody 60%, hba1c_change 50% (2026-08-22). Five of those six were never measured until the day they were fixed, and four of them had been publishing to the dashboard for months. The lesson is not "wildcards are bad" - it is that a pattern which has never had its OUTPUT read is an untested claim, and this repository kept treating untested claims as evidence. Second lesson, from the same run: extract_corpus_data.py was not in run_quality_improvements.py at all, so a 47/47 green pipeline could be built entirely on stale extraction. A green check on a step that was never run is worse than a red one.
doctrine_notes.2026_08_24_title_agreement: EXISTENCE, TOPIC, AND AGREEMENT ARE THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, AND THIS REPO HAD ONLY EVER ASKED THE FIRST TWO. validate_citations.py asks whether a PMID resolves. audit_path_citations.py / audit_citation_identifiers.py ask whether the resolved paper is roughly on-topic. Neither asks whether the paper is the one being described - even where the repo stores the description next to the PMID and could simply compare them. Of the 11 builder citation records carrying both a pmid and a title, 9 named a different paper; 6 were tagged GOLD or SILVER; all 9 were live on the published site. Four of the nine passed the topic screen because the wrong paper was also a diabetes paper, so the topic screen was never the control. RULE: wherever a claim and an identifier are stored together, compare them; a stored paraphrase that is never checked against its source is a latent false claim.
doctrine_notes.2026_08_24_do_not_widen_the_screen: WIDENING A SCREEN TO CLEAR A FAILURE IS THE SAME MOVE AS DELETING THE FAILURE. Two research_paths.json citations failed the DOMAIN screen and were correct (Murray/Wynn macrophage subsets; a CAD GWAS). Adding "macrophage" and "coronary" to DOMAIN would have cleared them and simultaneously lowered the gate for every future miscitation containing those words. They were recorded in topic_screen_exceptions.json with per-citation reasoning instead. Corollary recorded the same day: PMID 9742976 (UKPDS 33) was wrong for the LADA GADA claim and CORRECT in build_health_equity.py, so a PMID-keyed OFF-TOPIC badge would have replaced a false citation with a false badge. Verdicts about ATTACHMENTS must be scoped to the claim, not to the PMID.

pmid_magnitude_heuristic_2026_08_25.supersedes: the 'PMIDs above 42000000 are fabricated' rule in the scheduled-task file
pmid_magnitude_heuristic_2026_08_25.finding: The task file still instructs the credibility sweep to treat any PMID above 42000000 as fabricated. Measured live on 2026-08-25: NCBI esearch for 2026[dp] returns PMIDs up to 42626404, and this repo's own corpus now holds 30 PMIDs at or above 42000000, every one of which resolves. PMID 42608595 -- the highest-value new paper in today's queue, a real Diabetologia study from the Australian Islet Consortium -- would be destroyed by the rule as written. The threshold was already noted as stale on 2026-05-04; restating it here with a measured ceiling because the rule survives in the task file and will keep firing.
pmid_magnitude_heuristic_2026_08_25.replacement_rule: Do not reject a PMID by magnitude. Resolve it against NCBI esummary and compare the returned title with the title this repo asserts. Non-resolution is the fabrication signal; title DISAGREEMENT is the miscitation signal. A bare number threshold detects neither and, now that real PMIDs have crossed it, produces false positives on the newest and most valuable papers.

citation_defect_class_6_coordinates.name: INVENTED BIBLIOGRAPHIC COORDINATES
citation_defect_class_6_coordinates.statement: A citation can carry a resolving, on-topic, non-retracted PMID, be described accurately by the prose around it, and still assert a journal/volume/page coordinate that matches no PubMed record. The narrative is right and the numbers are invented, which is precisely the combination every prior gate passes: audit_prose_citation_titles scores the NARRATIVE, and the narrative is the true part.
citation_defect_class_6_coordinates.canonical_example: build_gka_lada.py published 'Diabetes. 2009 Jul;58(7):1416-28. PMID:19373249' under prose correctly describing Matschinsky's 2009 glucokinase review. PMID 19373249 is Nat Rev Drug Discov 2009;8(5):399-416. Diabetes vol 58 issue 7 exists and holds 34 articles; page 1416 is not among them.
citation_defect_class_6_coordinates.scale_on_first_run: 11 suspect of 94 coordinates, across build_gka_lada.py, build_data_dictionary.py, build_gka_landscape.py. After repair: 107/107 OK.
citation_defect_class_6_coordinates.method_note: A NEGATIVE probe result is what licenses the word NONRESOLVING, so the negative must be earned. PubMed's [ta] field indexes NLM abbreviations and only SOME full titles, and returns an empty idlist with NO phrasesnotfound error for the rest. Measured today: 'Nature Reviews Endocrinology'[ta] -> 3059 records, but 'Journal of Clinical Investigation'[ta] -> 0 and 'Trends in Endocrinology & Metabolism'[ta] -> 0, all three being real indexed journals. The gate's first draft called three build_data_dictionary.py citations NONRESOLVING on that basis - a verdict reached by a broken instrument, which would have remained 'true' after any repair. Fixed by running a positive control on the journal token before trusting any negative.

citation_defect_class_7_load_bearing.name: THE LOAD-BEARING CITATION
citation_defect_class_7_load_bearing.statement: One real, on-topic, correctly-cited source attached to many distinct quantitative claims it does not contain. Every individual instance passes every gate, because every gate asks about the PAPER. This class is only visible when you ask about the CLAIM.
citation_defect_class_7_load_bearing.canonical_example: PMID 34763823 (Herman WH & Kuo S, '100 years of Insulin: Why is Insulin So Expensive and What Can be Done to Control Its Cost?', Endocrinol Metab Clin North Am 2021;50(3S):e21-e34) is cited 91 times across 91 DISTINCT claim contexts, including GLP-1 agonist pricing, SGLT2i launch pricing, GKA generic projections to 2042-2045, drug development cost ($2.6B / $300M), CGM device cost, verapamil therapy cost, and the December 2024 Hikma semaglutide generic launch. It is a review of INSULIN pricing published in 2021.
citation_defect_class_7_load_bearing.automatable_part: TEMPORAL IMPOSSIBILITY is fully objective and is what the gate fails on: a paper cannot report an event that post-dates it. Restricted to RETROSPECTIVE claims - the first draft flagged a 2023 GBD paper projecting to 2050, which is what a GBD paper is for. Two filters are required together: the claim year must not be in the future, and the claim must not be phrased as a forecast.
citation_defect_class_7_load_bearing.judgement_part: Citation CONCENTRATION is reported, never failed. A landmark trial is legitimately cited often and the count alone cannot separate the two cases. Top concentrations measured today: 34763823 (91), 29710129 CAR-T costs (81), 37909353 (47), 32175717 (39).

pmid_ceiling_is_not_a_constant.supersedes: the 'PMIDs above 42000000 are fabricated' rule in the scheduled-task file
pmid_ceiling_is_not_a_constant.statement: Re-confirmed independently today, two days after the 2026-08-25 note. The live PubMed ceiling measured by esearch sort=most+recent is 42,649,123, up from 42,626,404 on 2026-08-25 - roughly 11k new PMIDs per day. Both repo PMIDs above the old threshold resolved and matched their logged titles exactly: 42608595 (Rogers NM, Diabetologia 2026, belatacept/sirolimus islet transplantation) and 42631883 (Elsayed MS, Mol Biol Rep 2026, rat myocardial injury). The sweep must compare against a ceiling QUERIED AT RUNTIME, never a hardcoded constant, or it will manufacture false fabrication reports at an accelerating rate.

gates_must_not_be_silenced_by_filename.statement: Wiring audit_citation_coordinates.py into the pipeline made it report, on its first run, the COMMENT in run_quality_improvements.py that documents why it exists - because that comment necessarily quotes the fabricated coordinate. The tempting fix, skipping audit_*.py and the runner by filename, would have opened a blind spot in files that also carry real citations. Instead the opt-out is an explicit CITATION-EXAMPLE marker written next to the example, so every suppression is visible in the diff and greppable. Exactly one exemption exists in the repo today. Silence must be requested by name, never inherited from a filename.

doctrine_notes.membership_is_two_questions: Asked on 2026-08-28 after FLAGGED was found to mean two incompatible things at once. "May this PMID be cited?" and "May it count as evidence?" are different questions and a single boolean answers neither well. PMID 18662538 (Massague, TGFbeta in Cancer, Cell 2008) is cited correctly as the definitional source for a data-dictionary term and supplies no diabetes finding: both facts have to survive. corpus_membership.py owns the distinction; nothing else may re-implement it.
doctrine_notes.count_never_answers_of_what: The four highest-ranked live research paths by data-point count all rest on no primary data: ranks 1 and 2 on a meta-analysis whose extracted numbers cannot be attributed to the pooled estimate, ranks 4 and 5 on a clinical trial PROTOCOL. Ranking by count is therefore inversely related to evidence quality at the top of this dashboard. Publication type is the cheapest honest answer and it comes from PubMed, not from local regexes.
doctrine_notes.absence_from_a_synthesis_is_not_evidence: PMID 40598585 (BMC Med 2025 network meta-analysis) names 11 interventions that beat placebo on 12-month C-peptide and verapamil is not among them. That is because the review covers IMMUNOTHERAPIES and verapamil was never eligible for inclusion. Reading a scope exclusion as a negative result is a mistake this corpus is well placed to make and must not.

citation_correct_claim_unsupported.rule: A citation that resolves, names the right author, year and title can still be the wrong source. Identifier gates cannot detect this. Before trusting a repeated citation, read what the cited paper is ABOUT and compare it to the sentence it supports.
citation_correct_claim_unsupported.instance: PMID 29710129 (CAR-T cost letter) sourcing 47 generic-drug price claims

pubtype_absence_is_not_evidence.rule: PubMed publication type is trustworthy when present and silent when absent. Absence is not "unknown but probably fine" - 37% of this corpus and 66% of its 2026 papers have no design tag. Any grade built on pubtype must publish its own coverage.

watch_item_recheck_dates_are_not_self_ex.note: Three watch items carried next_recheck dates of 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13 and sat untouched for 18-41 days while eight daily runs went past them. All three resolved on the first attempt with a single DOI query. A date field that nothing reads is a reminder nobody receives. RECOMMENDED: fold watch_items_pending_pmid into the work queue proper so overdue items surface the way queue items do, rather than living in a side list.

doctrine_notes.nct_identifiers_2026_09_01: Trial registry identifiers are citations and are gated like citations. A resolvable NCT is not a supported NCT. Repair only against a registry record fetched live; where no substitute is verified, mark UNSOURCED and invent nothing (the 2026-08-29 rule, extended from PMIDs to NCTs).
doctrine_notes.2026-09-02: Two failure modes, both about labels that assert verification without carrying it. (1) A hand-written '# --- VERIFIED: ...' comment is not verification. build_trial_equity_mapper.py carries that marker on every entry; six of its entries disagreed with ClinicalTrials.gov, four of them pointing at trials in unrelated specialties (a TAVI cardiology study, a postpartum-haemorrhage trial, an acute spinal-cord-injury study, a hidradenitis suppurativa dermatology trial). The gate that caught them, audit_nct_identifiers.py, has existed since 2026-08-29; nothing had made it green. Rule: a VERIFIED marker written by a human or by an earlier run means nothing unless a gate re-derives it. (2) A gap slot number is not a gap identity. Gap #15 accumulated seven audits of a topic that was not Gap #15, and a promotion_candidate flag with it, because nothing checked the audit note against the canonical gap name. Every gap audit should now open by restating the canonical name from build_data_dictionary.py GAPS before searching.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-03: A NUMBER COPIED INTO FOUR FILES IS NOT A FACT, IT IS FOUR FACTS THAT HAPPEN TO AGREE FOR A WHILE. Two findings, one cause. (1) NUMBERING. On 2026-09-02 a run found gaps["15"] had been auditing SGLT2i x personalized nutrition since April while canonical Gap #15 is GKA Pricing, and queued a re-homing of that one trail. Sweeping all fifteen the same way finds FIVE more: state #4, #5, #7, #11 and #12 each answer a question their number does not name, every one of them internally consistent back to April. Nothing drifted. Two numbering schemes were built independently and never reconciled. The lesson is not about gaps: when a run finds one instance of a defect, the next question is always how many instances the same measurement would find, and the 2026-09-02 run stopped at one. (2) TIER. The gap tier is hardcoded in 24 places across 15 gaps and read from the evidence store in none of them - agent_state.json, gap_evidence.json, the card text in rebuild_website.py and the stage labels in run_quality_improvements.py all carry their own typed copy. Three gaps already disagree: #6 and #11 are GOLD in memory and in the store but publish as SILVER, #13 was SILVER in memory against BRONZE everywhere else. Memory was corrected down for #13 because it was the optimistic outlier; #6 and #11 go to the human queue because raising a published tier is a scientific judgement, not a reconciliation. GENERAL RULE ADOPTED: any value that appears on the published site and also in the agent memory must have exactly one writer and be read from it, or be gated. Gap tiers are now gated by Analysis/Scripts/audit_gap_numbering.py; they are not yet single-writer.
doctrine_notes.path_verdict_key_split_2026_09_05: validated_paths records store their verdict under TWO different keys. Census 2026-09-05 of 67 records: 37 carry 'rating' only, 10 carry 'status' only, 20 carry both. path_store.py:142 and audit_citation_identifiers.py:256 already read both defensively, which is why nothing has broken yet. But a new consumer reading only 'rating' silently loses 10 of 67 paths (15%) and one reading only 'status' loses 37 of 67 (55%), and in both cases the loss reads as 'never validated'. This is the same shape as the 2026-08-16 defect where two path stores used different key spellings and emitted six false NEVER-VALIDATED work items. Not urgent - no live consumer is affected - but it should be normalised to one key before a consumer is written that is not defensive.
doctrine_notes.mount_unlink_blocked_2026_09_05: The workspace mount is FUSE and forbids unlink REPO-WIDE: rm returns 'Operation not permitted' on any path, including .git/index.lock and .git/HEAD.lock. git therefore cannot clear its own locks, and every run since April has worked around it by RENAMING them - ~180 orphaned .git/*.lock.* files have accumulated since 2026-04-10 under a dozen ad-hoc naming schemes (.bak, .del, .gone, .stale_<epoch>, .z_<nanos>). It has never been written down as a known constraint, so each run rediscovers it. Two consequences worth keeping: (a) rename is permitted where unlink is not, which is the standing workaround; (b) any code whose correctness depends on a delete succeeding is broken here - that is exactly why gap_analysis_daily.py's checkpoint expiry had to move to the read path.

2026-09-07.scope_artifact_absence: AN ABSENCE INSIDE ANOTHER STUDY'S INCLUSION CRITERIA IS NOT AN EVIDENCE GAP. Caught today in PMID 40598585: a network meta-analysis restricted by design to immunomodulatory RCTs was being read as evidence that nutrition has not been trialled. Before any "X was absent from Y" claim is published, read Y's inclusion criteria and confirm X was ELIGIBLE and MISSING rather than EXCLUDED. Candidate gate: flag any absence claim whose supporting citation is a systematic review, since SRs always have inclusion criteria that manufacture absences.
2026-09-07.pmcid_pmid_dedup_blind_spot: The intake path can log a paper already in the corpus as a novel external find when the source gives a PMCID and the corpus is keyed on PMID. Happened with PMC12211534 = PMID 40598585 (already VETTED). Fix: resolve every PMCID to a PMID at intake, before the novelty check.
2026-09-07.absence_claims_need_a_search_not_a_citat: Gap #11 rated GOLD for months on two papers that were not about its question. The evidence for "nobody has studied X" is a dated, reproducible query string and its hit count - not a citation. Any gap whose evidence list contains only papers that do not mention the gap's own subject should fail a gate.
2026-09-07.dorzagliatin_convergence: Three separately-tracked items are the same molecule: NCT06976658 (Phase 2, monogenic diabetes, CUHK), PMID 42014686 (Phase I DDI with empagliflozin), and the GKA paths under canonical Gaps #7 and #15. They should be reconciled before the GKA line is presented as several independent threads.
2026-09-07.intersection_evidence: EVERY GAP HERE IS AN INTERSECTION, AND EVIDENCE FOR ONE AXIS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THE GAP. Measured 2026-09-07 across all 15 gaps: 9 fail. The recurring shape is a pile of papers on the easy axis (LADA epidemiology, islet transplant outcomes, GKA trials) standing in for the hard axis (gene therapy, equity, repurposing) that makes the gap a gap. Half-covered evidence is the most dangerous kind because a human skimming the citation list sees on-topic papers and stops. Rule: a gap's tier may not exceed what its evidence covers on its WEAKER axis.

doctrine_notes.verification_can_launder_an_unchecked_fi: 2026-09-16. A verification pass that confirms the part of a citation it set out to check can certify the parts it did not. On 2026-09-14 the CONTENTS of PMID 37359825 were verified against its abstract and found correct; the SURNAME was copied from the prose being audited, never checked, and then written into agent_state.json as 'Not a defect - the CORRECT source'. That record would have made every subsequent sweep skip the file. RULE: a verification record must name which fields were checked and against what. A field not named is NOT verified, and no 'not a defect' note may be written about a citation whose author, title, journal and identifier were not each independently resolved.
doctrine_notes.unknown_buckets_are_selected_not_neutral: 2026-09-16. A gate that declines to judge what it cannot look up is not being conservative if the unlookuppable set is SELECTED for risk. A PMID is missing from the paper library precisely when it was added recently and by hand, which is when it is most likely to be wrong. The surname gate's UNKNOWN bucket held 16 attributions and one of them was a live defect that had already been certified as correct. RULE: before treating an unknown bucket as benign, ask what puts an item IN it. If the answer correlates with the defect being hunted, the bucket must be resolved, not excused.
doctrine_notes.a_gate_red_at_its_own_reflection_is_a_de: 2026-09-16. Every one of the credibility sweep's five findings was its own detection patterns, quoted inside the per-run verify_*_repairs.py scripts. A gate that reports red every run for a reason nobody acts on stops being read - the documented way eleven push notices decayed into background noise in this repo. RULE: when a gate fails, check whether it is looking at the repository or at the gate. Self-exclusion is by path or name CLASS, never by enumerated filename, so tomorrow's instance is covered the day it is written.
doctrine_notes.diagnose_the_forbidden_operation_not_the: 2026-09-16. For seven runs this agent recorded 'git is unwritable from the sandbox' and escalated it as a P0 needing a Windows-side Remove-Item. The diagnosis was one level too coarse and cost a week of invisible work. What is forbidden on the OneDrive mount is UNLINK, and only unlink: creating files under .git works, and so does rename. Git's lock protocol is create X.lock, write, rename X.lock -> X - all permitted. Only the CLEANUP of a lock left by an interrupted run needs unlink. GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed outside the mount avoids index.lock entirely; HEAD.lock can be renamed aside. Both commits today were made this way. RULE: when a tool fails on a mount, identify which SYSCALL is refused before concluding the tool cannot be used. Encoded in Analysis/Scripts/sandbox_git_commit.sh so it is not rediscovered by hand a thirteenth time - the .git directory already holds a dozen HEAD.lock.* files from prior runs working this out and not writing it down.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-17_compile_before_content: A gate that checks the CONTENT of an assertion cannot see a file that does not run. build_gap_deep_dives.py was syntactically invalid AT HEAD for a full day and its dashboard was frozen while seven correction passes edited the source. Cheapest possible check, zero false positives, now the first pipeline stage. COROLLARY WORTH NAMING: this project's habit of pasting the replaced text, in quotes, into a correction note inside a string literal is exactly what produces unescaped quotes. The more carefully a run documents a repair, the likelier it is to break the file it is repairing.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-17_unknown_bucket_is_the_yield: The trial-phase gate found ZERO live mismatches and the run's four real defects all came out of its UNKNOWN bucket. A gate's flagged list is not its output; the list of things it could not decide is where the work is. Resolving unknowns must be part of the gate's job, not a follow-up item.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-17_first_measurement_measures_th: The trial-phase gate's first run reported 5 mismatches. ALL FIVE were gate defects: the resolver read phases out of papers' BIBLIOGRAPHIES via efetch, assigned phases to Reviews and Letters that have none, and bound a phase to a PMID when it belonged to an NCT in the same sentence. Fifth run: 0 flagged, and the known-positive test still fires. Measure-before-wiring has now stopped five bad gates.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-17_a_tool_reporting_success_is_n: The index-resync step added today printed 'resynced to HEAD (status is truthful again)' while git status still showed 35 staged deletions: GIT_INDEX_FILE was still exported, so read-tree rewrote the throwaway index. The step reported on whether it RAN, not on whether the repository CHANGED. Every gate and repair in this project should be checked by re-measuring the thing it claims to have fixed, not by reading its own exit line - which is the same failure as the 2026-09-14 clearance record, in shell rather than in prose.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-18_gate_failing_on_correct_prose: A GATE FAILED THE PIPELINE ON TWO CITATIONS THE REPOSITORY HAD WRITTEN CORRECTLY, AND THE DISPROOF WAS IN THE GATE'S OWN OUTPUT. audit_citation_coordinates.py reported two live POINTS_ELSEWHERE: build_health_equity.py:1281 (PMID 36215990 asserted at Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2022;10(10):741) and verify_2026_09_13_repairs.py:37 (PMID 22336824 asserted at JAMA Oncol 2018;4(7):994). Both were artifacts of window cutting: the coordinate belongs to the PMID cited a few lines EARLIER in the same block (36113507 and 29710129 respectively), and the gate's own PROBE line said so verbatim - 'coordinate resolves to PMID 36113507' - while the gate failed anyway. It had computed the answer and not consulted it. FIX: harvest() now carries every other PMID within 800 chars; if the probe resolves the coordinate to one of them, the verdict is AMBIGUOUS_PAIRING - printed in full, never failed. This does not mask a real misattribution, because a fabricated coordinate resolves to a paper that is NOT cited nearby, and the neighbouring PMID's own coordinate is still harvested and checked independently. THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the third time a variant of this has been recorded here: WHEN A GATE FAILS, READ ITS OUTPUT BEFORE EDITING THE REPOSITORY. The obvious response to a red coordinate gate is to 'fix' the citation. Doing that here would have replaced two correct citations with two wrong ones and left the gate green - a silent corruption produced by obeying a gate.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-18_a_gate_with_no_live_positive: THE COMPUTED-VALUE GATE WAS BUILT AFTER ITS ONLY LIVE POSITIVE HAD ALREADY BEEN REPAIRED, WHICH MEANS A CLEAN RUN PROVES NOTHING. The 2026-09-13 defect (build_lada_diagnostic_model.py:763-766, a PMID inside the same f-string as an interpolated computed cost) was fixed before audit_computed_value_citations.py existed. A gate that has only ever returned zero is indistinguishable from a gate that does not work. Rather than trust the zero, the original defect was reproduced verbatim in _tmp_gate_known_positive.py, which the audit's own SKIP_PREFIXES excludes from normal runs and which is reachable only by calling scan_file() on it directly. Both lines are reported COMPUTED, confirmed 2026-09-18. EVERY GATE ADDED HERE FROM NOW ON SHOULD SHIP WITH A FIXTURE IT MUST CATCH, not just a live count it happens to clear.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-18_measure_first_earned_its_keep: THE COMPUTED-VALUE GATE'S FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS 13 HITS AND ALL 13 WERE FALSE. The first implementation asked only whether a PMID appeared anywhere in the same f-string - but the builders here write the ENTIRE page as one f-string, so {COLORS['bg']} at the top was flagged against a PMID four thousand characters below. Adding a 180-character proximity window took it to 4. Excluding verify_/check_/reconcile_ scripts, which print counts ABOUT PMIDs (f"{len(live_bad)} LIVE link(s) to PMID 34763823 remain") and are the opposite of the defect, took it to 1. Had this shipped as a gate on the first measurement it would have failed the pipeline on 13 non-defects and been switched off within a day. Standing instruction confirmed for the fourth time: MEASURE AND REPORT THE HIT COUNT BEFORE WIRING A GATE IN.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-18_a_gate_that_can_never_go_gree: The surname gate's four remaining mismatches after today's repairs were ALL in frozen archive - dated ACTION_REQUIRED and iterate_run_report markdown, and a _close_run script - where the 'mismatch' is this repository quoting a defect it had just fixed. One is literally a fenced HTML block showing the bad anchor. Those files are history and must not be rewritten; editing a dated run report to clear a gate is the failure this repo audits for. But left in the MISMATCH bucket they guarantee the count never reaches zero, and a gate that can never go green is a gate that gets ignored. Resolved with a SURFACE SPLIT, not an exclusion: every finding is still printed and still written to the JSON; only the headline count and the --gate exit code are scoped to the live publishing surface. Deliberately NOT done: adding loose strings to CORRECTION_MARKERS. The note at the top of that tuple warns against exactly that, because a marker silences a class of finding everywhere, whereas a surface split silences nothing.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-19: A citation gate that only compares a PMID to the words next to it cannot see a wrong-SUBJECT citation, because the words next to it were written from the same wrong paper. Both 2026-09-19 defects were internally consistent and externally false. The check that works asks a question neither the prose nor the PMID can answer alone: does the cited paper mention the thing this record is ABOUT. Second lesson, from the index bug: a summary count and the records it summarises are two independent assertions about the same fact, and this repository had never compared any pair of them. A lookup that silently misses produces well-formed empty fields and a confident metadata line, which is indistinguishable from success unless something checks the file against itself. Third lesson, from the eviction: a gate written for one bug caught a different and worse one within an hour, because arithmetic does not care what you were looking for. The cheapest checks in this repository have consistently been the ones that compare a file to itself. Fourth: a workaround that makes the first command succeed can hide which command was actually failing. Three runs treated this as an index-lock problem because GIT_INDEX_FILE made `git add` work; the lock git could not take was HEAD.lock.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-20: A GATE THAT NAMES ITS OWN MISSING ENFORCEMENT IS NOT ENFORCED. corpus_membership.py contained, in its own source, both the rule ("a FLAGGED paper with no membership_class is a bug, not a default") and the remedy ("an audit fails on this") - and the audit did not exist. The docstring read as if it did, which is worse than silence: it made every reader of that module, human and agent, believe the check was running. Two of the three defects found today were of this form. THE TEST TO APPLY: for every invariant a module DESCRIBES, grep for a caller of the function that checks it. A documented invariant with zero call sites is a comment. citable() had zero call sites while the site cited four papers it answered False for. SECOND, NARROWER RULE, and it generalises past membership: EXCLUSION AND DELETION MUST NOT SHARE A PREDICATE. Excluding a record is reversible and its reason can be re-read tomorrow; deleting it leaves nothing to reverse. So deletion must require an affirmative adjudication and must never be triggered by the ABSENCE of one. The 2026-09-19 eviction ledger recorded a blank field as the justification for removing three primary human studies, and it was internally consistent while doing so.

doctrine_notes.verification_method_2026-09-21: VERIFY THE CLAIM, NOT THE EDIT. A repair verified by grepping for the strings you just wrote is self-confirming: it proves the edit landed and is structurally incapable of finding another copy of the same falsehood elsewhere. On 2026-09-21 that method returned a clean result while the identical fabrication was live in three other builders and both published dashboard copies. The test that works starts from the ASSERTION -- drug, number, endpoint -- and sweeps the whole corpus for anything that states it, however worded. Corollary, learned the same day: a NEW GATE MUST BE TESTED FOR ITS EXIT CODE, not just its printed verdict. This one printed [FAIL] and returned 0 for its entire first life.
doctrine_notes.2026-09-22: A green stage count is evidence about the stages, not about the repository, and today it was wrong in two independent ways at once: a gate whose verdict could not reach the runner, and a gate that examined one mention of each identifier and discarded the rest. Both produce the same artifact -- a confident [OK] beside an unexamined defect. The general rule this suggests, which the next run should test rather than assume: before trusting any gate's green, ask what it would take for that gate to be INCAPABLE of red, and check that the number of things it examined matches the number of things there are. Today those two questions were worth twelve live defects.

closed_queue_items.target: RE-FRAME BARICITINIB ON THE STRENGTH OF PMID 42627334 (Diabetes Care 2026, BANDIT post-treatment follow-up). Research_Findings_Summary currently lists baricitinib/BARICADE as BRONZE with "Phase 2 data promising; Phase 3 not yet enrolled". The new paper reports that the benefit WANES: C-peptide significantly greater at week 72 (0.54 vs 0.38 pmol/mL, P=0.015) but not at week 96 (P=0.336), no differences in insulin dose, HbA1c or CGM measures during follow-up, and the CD8+ effector memory changes seen at week 48 had resolved by week 96. The authors conclude durable benefit likely requires continuous treatment. There is also an age split worth carrying: adults (n=28) fully preserved beta-cell function after stopping, children (n=32) declined (P=0.022) - note this is POST HOC. "Promising" without "wanes off-treatment" is the kind of half-summary this repo keeps catching elsewhere.

Neither is an equity analysis. Both establish that the registry EXISTS and reports graft outcomes. Nothing in either paper bears on race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status or access. An absence claim cannot be evidenced by two papers that are not about the thing claimed absent - it needs a documented search that returns nothing. Until today no such search had been run.

finding_2_the_gap_itself_survives_testin.confidence: LIKELY (not certain - see scope limit below)

The set is dominated by other fields: 35845323 racial disparities in LIVING DONOR KIDNEY transplant; 36566139 kidney organ allocation fairness; 42548012 xenotransplantation consensus; 41694652 global aortic aneurysm mortality; 42626230 pancreatic nerve anatomy across species; 36328836 cardiorenal clinical complexity; 39229679 pediatric donor pancreas-kidney utilisation; 42488823 ATMP bioengineering; 40668408 monogenic diabetes; 33444224 beta-cell function review.
Full PMID list retrieved. No record is titled on equity, disparity, race, ethnicity or access. The CITR output line is graft function, C-peptide, HLA matching, hypoglycaemia and registry updates.

finding_2_the_gap_itself_survives_testin.statement_that_is_supportable: As of 2026-09-07 there is no PubMed-indexed analysis of equity - racial, ethnic or socioeconomic - in access to or outcomes of islet transplantation, including in the 31 PubMed-indexed papers drawing on the Collaborative Islet Transplant Registry.
finding_2_the_gap_itself_survives_testin.statement_that_is_NOT_supportable: That no such analysis exists. CITR annual reports, NIDDK data-request outputs, conference abstracts and theses are grey literature and are not indexed the way these searches index. The claim must be scoped to "PubMed-indexed" every time it is published. This is why the confidence is LIKELY, not CERTAIN.
finding_2_the_gap_itself_survives_testin.path_to_certain: Read the CITR Annual Report scientific summaries directly (citregistry.org) and search Embase + conference proceedings. Neither was reachable this run.

finding_3_mechanistic_hypothesis.implication_if_it_holds: Islet transplantation would have a mechanistically predicted equity problem that has never been measured - which is a sharper and more testable version of Gap #11 than the gap as currently written.
finding_3_mechanistic_hypothesis.what_would_falsify_it: Any CITR stratification showing recipient race/ethnicity distribution matching the T1D population; or evidence that HLA-DR matching plays no role in islet allocation in practice.
finding_3_mechanistic_hypothesis.next_step: Read 37026004 in full and check whether it reports recipient race/ethnicity at all. That single fact decides whether this hypothesis is testable from published data or needs a CITR data request.

interpretation.headline: Gap #11 was not an isolated defect. 9 of 15 gaps fail. The hub has been assigning evidence tiers to intersections while storing evidence for only one side of the intersection.

hard_failures.meaning:
The stored evidence is about a DIFFERENT SUBJECT. Verified by reading the stored titles directly, not just the regex verdict:
  #1 Gene Therapy for LADA, SILVER, 31 papers - every one is a LADA autoantibody/phenotype/prevalence study (GAD affinity, ICA titres, Action LADA, C-peptide screening). ZERO concern gene therapy, vectors, AAV, CRISPR or gene transfer. The gap is rated on LADA epidemiology.
  #11 Islet Transplant Registry Equity, GOLD, 2 papers - the 2008 CITR update and a graft-function cohort. Neither mentions equity, race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status or access.
  #13 Personalized Nutrition for Beta Cells, BRONZE, 3 papers - all three are berberine trials in TYPE 2 DIABETES for glycaemic control and dyslipidaemia. Berberine is a plant-derived alkaloid drug, not personalized nutrition, and none of the three is about beta-cell preservation. This is a mis-file, not merely a thin evidence base.

soft_failures.meaning: HUMAN CALL, and the gate should not decide it. #4 (Drug Repurposing for Islet Transplant) cites anakinra, etanercept and rapamycin in islet transplant; #7 (GKA Drug Repurposing) cites dorzagliatin trials and GKA meta-analyses. Those drugs ARE repurposed agents. But no cited paper FRAMES itself as repurposing, so what these gaps have is evidence of the drugs, not evidence about the repurposing question. Whether that counts is a scientific judgement about what the gap claims.

zero_evidence_tiers.meaning: BRONZE with zero papers. A tier above EXPLORATORY asserts evidential standing neither gap has. Gap #9 holds zero papers too but is correctly labelled EXPLORATORY and does not fail.

inference_only.meaning: #8 Immunomodulatory Drugs for LADA, 27 papers: 7 touch immunomodulation, 15 touch LADA, and NOT ONE touches both. The intersection is joined by inference across papers rather than evidenced by any of them. That may be defensible - it may even be the point of the gap - but it must be stated, not implied by a citation list.

2026-09-07.what_this_gate_does_not_prove: It reads stored titles and finding snippets only; it fetches no abstracts. A miss is an UPPER bound on the problem and a prompt to read the paper, not a proven defect. And passing is weak news: one passing mention of a word is not an analysis. The three hard failures above were confirmed by reading the stored titles by hand, which is why they are stated as fact and the rest are stated as flags.
2026-09-07.not_applied: No tier was changed and no gap was deleted by this run. Nine simultaneous demotions is a scientific judgement about the hub's own headline claims, and the 2026-09-03 single-writer refactor has not landed, so a tier written now would fork further.
